observed.title: Commit the external delivery record unconditionally; keep trigger bookkeeping best-effort
observed.statement: When an externally-delivered event (webhook) and its trigger's metadata share a transaction, insert the durable event record FIRST and treat a lost CAS on the trigger's version bump as a logged no-op — never discard a legitimately-received external delivery over a benign metadata race.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs` `mark_triggered_and_publish` — the `persona_events` INSERT commits unconditionally (a genuine DB error aborts and surfaces as HTTP 500 so the sender retries), while the `UPDATE persona_triggers ... WHERE trigger_version = ?` CAS returning 0 rows is logged (`trigger_version conflict ... event published, skipping best-effort metadata bump`) and the transaction still commits. The doc comment explicitly records the prior failure mode: a concurrent burst or scheduler tick advancing the version used to drop the event entirely.

observed.title: Run the constant-time HMAC compare even when the signature hex is invalid
observed.statement: In an HMAC verifier, substitute a dummy digest when hex-decoding the supplied signature fails, run the constant-time comparison anyway, and AND the result with the hex-validity flag — so valid-hex and invalid-hex signatures take the same timing path.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs` `verify_hmac_sha256` — `let dummy = [0u8; 32]` on hex-decode failure, then `mac.verify_slice(&expected_bytes).is_ok() && hex_valid` with a comment naming the timing side-channel this prevents. The verifier is exposed `pub(crate)` so the smee relay reuses it instead of duplicating crypto. Unit tests cover valid, `sha256=`-prefixed, and non-hex inputs.

observed.title: Never log a plaintext duplicate of a payload you encrypt at rest
observed.statement: When an inbound payload is encrypted before persistence, do not also write the identical raw body into a request/audit log table in plaintext — redact the logged body to a pointer at the encrypted durable copy, keeping headers and status for diagnostics.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs` `handle_webhook` — the persona_event payload is encrypted via `crypto::encrypt_for_db`, and the webhook request log stores `"[redacted: see encrypted persona_event payload]"` instead of the body, with a comment noting inbound webhooks routinely carry secrets/PII (GitHub payloads, third-party tokens) and that a plaintext log copy would undermine the at-rest encryption. Related: `src-tauri/engine/src/cli_mcp_config.rs` removed a dead second plaintext copy of run secrets in `settings.json` for the same reason.

observed.title: Reject out-of-window deliveries with 422 + Retry-After, and document the window on a GET
observed.statement: An ingestion endpoint with an availability window should reject out-of-window deliveries with a retryable status (422) carrying a Retry-After header computed to the next window open, and expose a GET on the same route that reports window state without leaking internal metadata — so machine senders can back off correctly and humans can debug.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs` — `process_webhook` returns `422 UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` with a `retry-after` header from `seconds_until_next_open` when a trigger's active window excludes now; `webhook_info` (GET on the same `/webhook/{trigger_id}` path) reports `has_active_window` / `currently_active` / `retry_after_seconds` plus a note describing the 422 behavior, and 404s non-webhook triggers rather than describing them.

observed.title: Drain relayed items oldest-first, pair each publish with its watermark atomically, and stop the lane on first failure
observed.statement: A poll-based relay must sort fetched items oldest-first, persist each item and its advanced watermark in ONE transaction, and on a publish failure break that source's loop so the watermark holds at the last contiguous success — a later success advancing past a failed item strands it forever.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/cloud_webhook_relay.rs` — firings are sorted ascending by parsed `fired_at` with a comment citing the incident (`bug-hunt 2026-06-07 cloud-sync #4`: a later success advanced the watermark past a failed firing and silently lost it); `publish_and_upsert_watermark` inserts the persona_event and upserts `cloud_webhook_watermarks` in a single SQLite transaction so restart cannot produce divergence; the per-trigger loop `break`s on error, holding the watermark and retrying next poll in order.

observed.title: A stream source that replays history on reconnect needs a cross-reconnect dedupe with a tiered key
observed.statement: When a push source (SSE, message replay service) re-sends recent history on every new connection, keep a bounded FIFO dedupe that SURVIVES reconnects, keyed by the best available delivery identity in tiers (protocol event id > provider delivery header > content hash), and send the last seen id (Last-Event-ID) on reconnect so a compliant server resumes instead of replaying.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/smee_relay.rs` `RelayDedup` — bounded VecDeque+HashSet (CAP 512) held OUTSIDE the reconnect loop so smee.io's history replay after laptop sleep / Wi-Fi drop doesn't re-spawn duplicate persona executions (comment cites `bug-hunt 2026-06-07 triggers #1`); dedup key tiers: SSE `id:` line, else `x-github-delivery`, else a hash of the data; `last_event_id` is replayed as the `Last-Event-ID` request header on reconnect.

observed.title: Reset reconnect backoff only after the connection proved stable
observed.statement: Do not reset exponential reconnect backoff on every clean disconnect — reset it only when the connection stayed alive past a minimum stability threshold, or a server that accepts TCP then immediately closes (rate limiting) turns your backoff into a reconnect storm.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/smee_relay.rs` — `MIN_STABLE_CONNECTION_SECS: u64 = 30` with the comment 'Prevents reconnect storms when the server accepts TCP then immediately closes (e.g., rate limiting)'; the reconnect loop only does `backoff = Duration::from_secs(1)` when `connected_at.elapsed() >= MIN_STABLE_CONNECTION_SECS`, otherwise the doubling backoff (capped 30s) keeps growing across accept-then-close cycles.

observed.title: Fingerprint a live worker's config and restart the task when the fingerprint drifts
observed.statement: A manager loop that reconciles long-lived worker tasks (one per DB row) should store a serialized fingerprint of each worker's effective config at spawn time and cancel/respawn any worker whose row's current fingerprint differs — otherwise config edits made while a connection is alive silently never apply.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/smee_relay.rs` — `relay_config_key()` serializes (channel_url, target_persona_id, event_filter, allowed_repos) to JSON; `ActiveRelayTask.config_key` stores it; the sync pass stops tasks whose stored key differs from the freshly computed desired key ('Stopped Smee relay task for config sync') before starting replacements. Cancellation is token-based with a 2s grace then `abort()`.

observed.title: Name which filters are routing conveniences and which are security controls — and log the unauthenticated posture loudly
observed.statement: When an ingest path has both forgeable routing filters and a real authenticity gate, document at every touchpoint which is which, and when the authenticity gate is not configured, emit a loud, specific warning stating exactly what an attacker can do — never let a routing filter masquerade as authentication.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/smee_relay.rs` — `allowed_repos` is annotated '(NOT a security control)' at the struct field, at the filter site, and in the startup warning, because `body.repository.full_name` is attacker-controllable; the opt-in HMAC gate (`PERSONAS_SMEE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) fails closed when configured; when unset, each relay task logs: 'inbound events are NOT authenticated — the channel URL is an unauthenticated bearer credential... Anyone who learns the URL can inject events that spawn persona executions.' The comment notes the previous warning wrongly implied allowed_repos restricted origins.

observed.title: A skipped tick advances the schedule pointer but must never stamp 'last fired'
observed.statement: When a scheduler skips due work (outside active hours, gated, backing off), advance only the next-due pointer — writing the 'last triggered/fired' column on a skip makes the UI report a fire that never happened.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/polling.rs` `poll_one_trigger` — the active-window skip calls `trigger_repo::advance_schedule_pointer` and the comment spells out why not `mark_triggered`: 'The UI's "Last triggered" label (TriggerList.tsx) reads that column for every trigger type... would stamp it with `now` even though no GET was ever made, making the trigger look like it fired when it didn't.' It also notes `background.rs` mirrors the same split for schedule-type triggers, so the two write paths (pointer-only vs fired+pointer) are a deliberate repo-level vocabulary.

observed.title: Sequence matching must consume events by positional cursor — one event can never satisfy two steps
observed.statement: When matching an ordered condition list against a time-sorted event window, advance a positional consumption cursor past each matched event instead of comparing timestamps inclusively — otherwise one physical event (or two same-timestamp events handled wrongly) satisfies adjacent steps and an N-step sequence fires on fewer than N events.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/composite.rs` `evaluate_sequence_detailed` — `next_search` index cursor, comment documenting the regression: 'The old `ts >= last_time` + search-from-index-0 let ONE physical event satisfy two adjacent steps... Consuming by index guarantees each event satisfies at most one step.' Regression tests pin both directions: `one_event_cannot_satisfy_two_steps` and `same_timestamp_distinct_events_fire` (positional consumption still allows two distinct events sharing a timestamp).

observed.title: Derive a suppression-cache's retention cutoff from the largest live window, not a constant
observed.statement: When pruning per-key state that consumers read over configurable windows, compute the retention cutoff from the maximum window currently configured across live rows — a hardcoded cutoff races any consumer whose window equals or exceeds it.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/composite.rs` cleanup — 'use max_window (the largest window_seconds across all composite triggers) as the retention cutoff so we never prune a suppression entry that a trigger still needs. Previously used a hardcoded 3600s which raced with triggers whose window_seconds == 3600.' The same cutoff is applied to the in-memory `last_fired` map and the persisted `composite_trigger_fires` table so the two tiers cannot diverge.

observed.title: Re-clamp persisted values at the point of use to the validator's ceiling
observed.statement: A bound enforced at create/update time must be re-applied defensively where the value is consumed — rows persisted before the guard existed, or edited directly in the store, otherwise drive unbounded work (full-table scans, unbounded look-backs) every tick.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/composite.rs` — both the max-window computation and the per-trigger window apply `.min(MAX_COMPOSITE_WINDOW_SECONDS)` with the comment: 'Clamp defensively to the same ceiling the create/update validator enforces — a row persisted before that guard existed (or edited directly in the DB) could otherwise drive an unbounded look-back and a full-table scan every tick.' The clamp reuses the validator's own constant so the two bounds cannot drift.

observed.title: A relevance threshold calibrated on identical-text fixtures never fires on real inputs
observed.statement: Avoid tuning a match/suggestion threshold against verbatim-copy fixtures: real paraphrased inputs score far below identical text under weighted overlap, so the feature silently never triggers. Calibrate against the realistic score band and write the band math into the constant's comment.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/recipe_matcher.rs` `SUGGESTION_THRESHOLD` — recalibrated 2026-06-29 from 0.90 → 0.40; the constant's comment derives the arithmetic: with name=0.6/desc=0.3/tags=0.1 weighted Jaccard, a strong-but-paraphrased intent lands at ~0.40–0.55, so the old 0.90 (set against identical-text fixtures) meant 'the suggestion chip effectively never rendered'. A `match_threshold_gate` test now pins both the verbatim case AND the paraphrase band the old bar dropped.

observed.title: Regenerate injected prompt sections idempotently: strip by marker, then merge under user-owned keys
observed.statement: Machine-generated sections inside a user-editable document (prompt, instructions) need (a) a stable marker so regeneration strips the prior copy up to the next section boundary before appending, and (b) merge semantics where existing/user-authored keys always win over freshly-derived ones — so re-derivation is idempotent and never clobbers tuning.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/recipe_parameters.rs` — `SECTION_MARKER = "## Capability Parameters"` used 'both to render and to strip a prior copy so re-injection is idempotent'; `strip_parameters_section` removes from the marker to the next `\n## `; `apply_to_instructions` strips-then-appends (and with no params just strips, handling capability removal); `merge_persona_parameters` inserts derived keys only when absent ('existing keys win (template-authored or user-tuned)').

observed.title: A dry-run reuses the real pipeline's validate stages but persists nothing
observed.statement: Build execution previews by running the production pipeline's exact validation stages (credential resolution, contract checks, prompt assembly) and stopping before the spawn stage — deliberately creating NO execution row, so previews stay out of every metric query, dashboard, and activity feed by construction rather than by filtering.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/dry_run.rs` module docs — 'Mirrors the runner's Validate stage... but stops short of SpawnEngine'; 'By design we do not create a persona_executions row... Skipping DB persistence keeps dry runs out of every existing metric query, dashboard, and activity feed — the simplest possible isolation from real execution metrics.' The trace goes to the existing log-file surface instead. Notably the credential pass intentionally uses the real `resolve_credential_env_vars`, so OAuth refreshes the real run would perform also happen ('a feature, not a side effect to avoid').

observed.title: Route pre-flight refusals through the same typed result and audit path as runtime failures
observed.statement: Early returns (rate-limited, unsupported, misconfigured, missing credentials) in an invocation pipeline must produce the SAME typed result shape and hit the SAME audit log as post-dispatch failures — a raw error escaping before dispatch renders as garbage in the UI and leaves a hole in the audit trail.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/tool_runner.rs` `early_failure` helper — comment cites the incident: 'A raw Err reaches the webview as a plain object that the panel used to render as "[object Object]" (2026-07-16 UAT blocker), and it skipped the audit log entirely.' Every pre-flight branch (builtin-tool unsupported, rate limit, credential failure, misconfigured kind) returns `Ok(ToolInvocationResult{success:false, error_kind, retryable,...})` and writes the tool audit row. Timeouts likewise surface as a typed `Timeout` kind with `retryable: true`, and the builtin case replaced a misleading 'misconfigured' with an honest 'runs inside persona executions' message.

observed.title: Fuzzy matching needs a length floor, uniqueness-gated prefix matches, and ambiguity as a verdict
observed.statement: When fuzzily matching user resources to declared requirements, (1) skip fuzzy modes entirely below a minimum name length so generic tokens ('api', 'db') can't match vacuously, (2) accept prefix matches only when exactly one candidate hits, and (3) return multi-match as a first-class 'ambiguous' state the user resolves — never auto-pick among plausible candidates.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/templates/sub_n8n/edit/connectorMatching.ts` — `MIN_FUZZY_LENGTH = 4` gates prefix/substring tiers; prefix match applies only when `prefixMatches.length === 1`. `credentialGapAnalysis.ts` builds the three-state verdict `ready | ambiguous | missing` per connector, with `ambiguousCandidates` carried so the picker can present the choice instead of silently binding the first hit.

observed.title: Link derived entities by index or identity, never by scanning display strings
observed.statement: When one derivation pass produces parallel collections (triggers and the connectors that own them), carry ownership as an index-aligned or id-based link at build time — reconstructing ownership later by searching human-readable descriptions for a name cross-links every service whose name is a substring of another.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/personas/parsers/workflowPipeline.ts` — `triggerServices` is built index-aligned with `triggers` 'so a connector can claim its triggers by identity instead of by scanning the human-readable description for its own name (which cross-linked any service whose name is a substring of another — "mail" claimed "gmail")'; connectors compute `related_triggers` from the aligned array, and synthetic fallback triggers get service `''` so they stay unclaimed by every connector.

observed.title: GitHub Actions YAML `on:` parses as a boolean `true` key
observed.statement: YAML 1.1 parsers read the bare key `on` as boolean true, so a parsed GitHub Actions workflow may carry its trigger block under the key `true` instead of `on` — detectors and transformers must check both.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/personas/parsers/workflowDetector.ts` `detectFromYaml` — `const hasOn = 'on' in parsed || parsed.true !== undefined; // YAML \`on:\` can parse as \`true:\` key`, with a further fallback that treats `jobs` + `runs-on` as strongly indicative when neither key survives.

observed.title: Filter consumer ownership inside the claim query itself
observed.statement: When multiple consumers share a pending-work table but own disjoint subsets, the ownership predicate belongs INSIDE the atomic claim statement — claiming broadly and releasing non-owned rows both churns the WAL every tick (the released rows keep their position and are re-claimed forever) and lets a full window of non-owned rows starve the owned ones behind them.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/db/src/repos/communication/events.rs` `claim_pending_headless` — `UPDATE ... WHERE e.status='pending' AND (e.target_persona_id IS NULL OR p.headless = 1) ... RETURNING *` via a LEFT JOIN on personas; the comment records the prior claim-then-release ping-pong ('the same 5 rows were re-claimed every 5s tick — ~11 wasted statements + WAL churn per tick') and the starvation where non-headless events blocked headless ones indefinitely while the windowed app was closed.

observed.title: An auto-remediation flag must refuse gaps outside its remediation power
observed.statement: A 'fix it for me' option may only proceed when every blocking gap is of the kind it can actually fix; if any gap is outside its power (a credential it cannot provision, an unverifiable requirement), refuse the whole operation with the concrete list — and after remediating, re-score so the returned verdict reflects the post-fix state.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/recipes/recipe_adoption.rs` `adopt_recipe_for_persona_inner` — `auto_setup` wires missing-but-catalogued tools, but when `missing_tools_addable` is empty the setup need is connector/credential wiring, so adoption is refused 'regardless of auto_setup, since auto_setup only wires tools and cannot provision a credential. This prevents seeding a persona that can't actually run the recipe on first use.' Tool wiring failures abort the whole adoption (no partial wiring), and eligibility is re-scored after auto-setup so the frontend shows `Eligible` rather than the stale pre-wiring verdict. Tests pin every branch including corrupt-requirements refusal.

observed.title: Serialize delete against execution on the same in-flight guard, and let a staleness TTL unwedge orphans
observed.statement: A destructive lifecycle operation (delete) must acquire the SAME in-flight guard its entity's execution paths hold — refusing rather than racing a live run — and its 'active runs block delete' check must exempt rows past a generous staleness TTL so a crash-orphaned 'running' row cannot wedge deletion forever.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/tools/automations.rs` — `delete_automation` takes the shared `INFLIGHT_TRIGGERS` guard that `trigger_automation`/`test_automation_webhook` hold (comment cites refactor-bughunt-2026-07-10 #4: a delete could slip through the check→delete window while a trigger fired an outbound webhook); then `count_active_runs(&db, &id, DELETE_STALE_RUN_TTL_SECS)` counts directly (no 50-row snapshot that could miss an older run) and ignores runs older than 30 min — 'well beyond any legitimate run's worst-case retry+backoff budget, so a genuinely live run still blocks delete while a dead running row can't wedge it forever.'

observed.title: Advancing a chain's control flow is not forwarding its data
observed.statement: In a step-chaining system, wiring B to run after A does not automatically give B A's output — treat payload forwarding as an explicit, tested flag on the link, or chains 'work' in demos while every downstream step runs blind.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/triggers/sub_studio/libs/studioCommit.ts` `draftLinkToTriggerInput` — sets `payload_forward: true` with the comment: 'The engine only injects `source_output` into the next step when this flag is true (engine/chain.rs); without it a Studio-built A->B chain advanced control flow but B received no upstream payload (UAT L1 F-CHAIN-NO-PAYLOAD-FORWARD).' Sibling evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/context_fidelity.rs` addresses the fan-in variant of the same blindness.

observed.title: Fan-in pipeline nodes need a deterministic all-predecessors context digest
observed.statement: When each pipeline node runs in a fresh process/context, passing only the latest predecessor's raw output silently drops every other upstream branch at fan-in points — build a deterministic (no extra model call) digest of ALL completed predecessors at a configurable fidelity and attach it alongside the primary input.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/context_fidelity.rs` module docs — 'resolve_node_input passes only the single latest predecessor's raw output... so a fan-in node (multiple predecessors) silently loses every upstream output but one'; the module builds an `## Upstream Context` preamble from all completed predecessors deterministically ('no extra LLM call') and attaches it as `upstream_context` next to the existing `pipeline_input`, at a configurable fidelity level.

observed.title: Checkpoint each agent-run stage as a git commit on a per-run branch
observed.statement: Agents mutating a real repository should commit every completed stage onto a dedicated per-run branch (with trailers carrying run id + stage), giving a run that goes sideways a clean rewind point and a fork-from-here recovery using plain git — with auto-maintenance and signing disabled so checkpoints stay fast and deterministic.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/git_checkpoint.rs` — module docs: agent runs previously had 'zero checkpointing — a run that goes sideways mid-task has no clean rewind'; each checkpoint is a commit on `personas/run/<run_id>` with trailers for run id + stage; the stage→SHA index lives in SQLite rather than a second branch; all git calls disable auto-maintenance and signing for determinism inside agent workspaces.

observed.title: Scrub run-scoped secret files on every exit path, and sweep stale copies before writing
observed.statement: A config file that embeds short-lived secrets in a reused (non-deleted) working directory must be scrubbed on EVERY run exit path — normal, error, cancel, timeout, kill — and the writer must also sweep any stale copy from a prior possibly-killed run before writing, as belt-and-suspenders.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/cli_mcp_config.rs` — the `--mcp-config` file embeds the `PERSONAS_API_KEY` bridge key and delegate API keys in plaintext inside a 'stable, reused per-persona temp dir that the runner never deletes, so the file MUST be scrubbed at run termination via `scrub_mcp_sidecar` on every exit path (normal, error, cancel, timeout, kill). `install_mcp_sidecar` also sweeps a stale config from a prior, possibly app-killed run before writing.' A historical note records deleting a dead duplicate write that left 'a second plaintext copy of the same secrets for no behavioral gain'.

observed.title: Probe a CLI's capabilities by reading only its init handshake, then kill it
observed.statement: To detect which tools/tiers a spawned agent CLI exposes on this machine and account, launch it with the production flag set, read only its session-init event (emitted before any model turn), then kill the child — a near-zero-cost, account-accurate capability probe that gates tier-dependent features.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/cli_capabilities.rs` — spawns a bounded `claude -p` mirroring the production `build_cli_args` flag set, reads the `system/init` event's tool/agent registry to learn whether tier-gated deep-fanout tools (`Workflow` is Max/Team) are available, and 'reads only until the system/init line, then kills the child — init is emitted at session start, before any LLM turn, so a probe costs ~$0.' Features that depend on gated tools gate on the probe result rather than assuming account parity.

observed.title: Split a schedule timeline at 'now': project the future, but ground the past only in run records
observed.statement: A calendar/timeline for scheduled work must never render past occurrences from the same projection that draws the future — past slots are matched against real execution records and unmatched slots render as 'unknown', revealing skips, rate-limits and downtime instead of faking successes.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/schedules/libs/useCronPreview.ts` `useCalendarEvents` — 'FUTURE fires are projected... PAST fires are grounded in reality, not health'; cron past slots are matched to `list_recent_schedule_runs` within a tolerance, unmatched slots render as `past-unknown`; interval triggers, 'whose past cadence can't be reconstructed after any downtime drift, contribute their real runs directly' (no fabricated backward walk). The history command's 168h/200-row cap is honored by letting older slots honestly render as unknown.

observed.title: Add a new liveness signal as corroboration that degrades to the old rule
observed.statement: When adding a new health signal to an existing liveness/staleness decision, wire it as corroboration only — it may veto or confirm the incumbent rules but never replaces a trigger — and make every rule fall back to exactly the pre-signal behaviour whenever the new evidence is unusable.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/stale.rs` adds screen-movement detection to a staleness ticker already driven by transcript growth + hooks. The module comment states the contract: *"Screen movement is a THIRD corroborating input, never a replacement: it can veto a `Stale` verdict … but it removes no existing trigger and every rule below degrades to exactly today's behaviour when the evidence is unusable."* `usable_activity()` returns `Option<ScreenActivity>` where `None` means "no usable evidence" (screen too small, sample older than the asking rule's window, first render has no predecessor) and *"every caller must then behave as it did before this signal existed."* The screen-frozen verdict additionally requires the silence to PERSIST across ticks via `SCREEN_SILENT_SINCE`, cleared "the instant any evidence is lost … so the verdict can never be reached on stale data." `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/screen_activity.rs` documents why byte-presence alone can't see "alive-looking but stuck" (a spinner produces bytes forever).

observed.title: Classify an ambiguous parked state with a typed verdict that may abstain
observed.statement: When one catch-all state (e.g. 'stale') conflates situations the operator handles differently, add a classifier that reads the authoritative artifact and returns a typed verdict including an explicit Unknown that keeps the incumbent decision — and map verdicts onto the EXISTING lifecycle rather than inventing new states.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/classify.rs`: *"'Stale' was one amber bucket holding three completely different situations … Nothing ever read the transcript, so the one place that actually knows what a session was doing when it stopped was never consulted."* `ParkedVerdict::{Done, Blocked(Question|Permission), Hung(MidTool), Unknown}` where Unknown is documented as *"a classifier that guesses is worse than one that abstains."* The ticker (`classify_pass` in `stale.rs`) maps Done onto the pre-existing `mark_finished` path, Blocked onto `AwaitingInput` with a typed reason, and Hung keeps the existing frozen reason — *"No new state machine — a new reading of the same one."* `verdict_token()` exports stable machine tokens (`blocked_question`, `hung_mid_tool`) so the UI paints distinctly "instead of string-matching prose", and screen cues (a rendered permission prompt) win over the transcript because that case *cannot* appear in the transcript.

observed.title: Give background-ticker cutoffs a three-tier override: env test knob > user tune > default
observed.statement: Every time-based cutoff in a background loop should resolve through an explicit precedence chain — env var for test harnesses, clamped user setting, built-in default — and the transition rules themselves should be pure functions so the timing logic is unit-testable without running the loop.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/stale.rs` — `effective_secs()`: *"Effective cutoff in seconds: env test knob > user-tuned override > default."* `env_secs()` documents that `PERSONAS_FLEET_STALE_SECS` etc. *"lets test harnesses shorten the staleness windows for fast observation … without waiting the production 6 min"*; user tunes are clamped (`STALE_TUNE_RANGE: (60, 3600)`) with rationale ("Stale below 1 min flaps while the user is composing; frozen below 30s false-positives on model latency gaps"). The decision logic is extracted into pure functions with documented rule tables — `staleness_transition()` ("Extracted so the rules are unit-tested"), `is_frozen_mid_run()`, `parse_limit_reset()` — each with in-file `#[cfg(test)]` coverage. Every constant carries its justification inline (`DEV_SESSION_STALL_MULTIPLIER = 8` — "a silent `cargo check` … routinely runs 5-15 minutes; at 2 min every such compile was reported frozen").

observed.title: Funnel every state emission through one choke point so cross-cutting concerns attach once
observed.statement: When multiple independent lanes can change an entity's state, force them all through a single emit function; debug logging, waiter wakeups, and durable persistence then attach to that one point and a new lane gets them for free — while a hand-rolled emit silently gets none.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/pty.rs` — `emit_session_state()`: *"Four lanes decide a session's state independently (hooks, the staleness ticker, the transcript watcher, the headless stream-json reader) and each used to build its own copy of this payload. Funnelling them here keeps the wire shape identical across lanes and … gives the fleet exactly one place where 'a session changed state' is observable … Add a new lane and it is logged for free; emit the event by hand and it silently isn't."* Three concerns ride the choke point: `debug_log::state_change` (shareable causal log), `wait::note_state_changed()` ("one bump here covers every transition without each lane knowing waiters exist"), and `persist::note_changed()` (durable mirror, "enqueue-only … a slow DB can never wedge a PTY reader"). `persist.rs` confirms the design: *"Writes piggyback the two existing emit points … nothing gets a private write path that could drift."*

observed.title: Rehydrate persisted sessions as an already-existing sleep state, not a new restore state
observed.statement: When adding crash-restart durability to an in-memory registry, restore rows into a state shape the system already knows how to wake (here: a 'dozing tombstone' — displayed state preserved, no process handle), so the existing resume path resurrects them with zero special-casing and no new UI state.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/persist.rs`: *"Rehydration reuses the existing doze concept: a restored row is a `dozing` tombstone — displayed state preserved, no `child_pid`, wakeable by selecting it (exactly what a session dozed by the resource floor looks like). No new UI state, no new wake path."* `inner_from_row()` zeroes `last_pty_output_ms` ("keeps the frozen-process check … from flagging a restored row as hung"), preserves `created_at_ms` ("grid slots stay where the operator left them"), and maps unparseable/mid-spawn states to `Stale` ("honest — 'we don't know, look at it' — and doze-compatible"). Round-trip + tombstone-shape are unit-tested (`rehydrated_row_is_a_wakeable_dozing_tombstone`). Companion: `recover_after_restart()` force-parks mid-task orphans to `AwaitingInput` BEFORE the first ticker pass so the auto-forget sweep can't strand real work, and deliberately does NOT auto-kill-and-resume ("matching a process to a session by cwd is ambiguous … too risky to fire unattended").

observed.title: Preserve abnormal exit-status bits — reinterpret, never saturate
observed.statement: When converting an OS exit status across integer widths, reinterpret the bit pattern (as-cast) instead of saturating; saturation destroys diagnostic codes like Windows NTSTATUS values and renders every abnormal exit as one meaningless number.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/pty.rs` `reaper_loop()`: *"ExitStatus::exit_code is u32 on Windows and is frequently an NTSTATUS (e.g. 0xC0000142 STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED …). REINTERPRET the bits as i32 rather than saturating to i32::MAX — the old saturation threw the real code away and rendered every abnormal exit as the meaningless 'code 2147483647', which is exactly why an exit read as 'vanished without warning'. The bit pattern round-trips back to the OS code (`as u32`) for display."* The shared `finalize_child_exit()` then always logs WHY a session ended, including `code_hex = format!("0x{:08X}", c as u32)` — closing the companion gap that "an abnormal death … left no breadcrumb at all."

observed.title: Encode automated TUI keystroke plans in readable notation with one chunk per key
observed.statement: When a program drives another program's TUI, represent keystroke plans in human-readable notation (`<Down><Space><CR>`) that compiles to byte chunks, and make chunk boundaries semantic — one write per key — because target TUIs distinguish a typed key from the same byte arriving inside a paste.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/keys.rs`: raw plans logged as `["\u{1b}[B", " ", "\r"]` were *"not legible in either artifact — [the failure] had to be reconstructed by driving a stuck session key-by-key over the bridge."* And chunking is load-bearing: *"Claude Code's composer distinguishes a typed Enter (a lone `\r` write) from a pasted one (a `\r` inside a larger write) — the latter inserts a soft line-break and does NOT submit. That distinction caused the 2026-07-24 incident where an auto-fired instruction sat unsubmitted in the composer until the doze pass reaped the session. `parse_plan` therefore emits one chunk per key, so a plan written in notation cannot accidentally collapse into a paste."* Literal text still coalesces into one paste chunk; the parser is kept even though production only builds plans, so plans and test expectations share one vocabulary.

observed.title: Capture timeout diagnostics inside the wait primitive itself, with a content-free shape for shareable logs
observed.statement: A wait/expect primitive should attach evidence (screen snapshot, raw tail, generation, lifecycle state, and an 'ended' flag distinguishing dead-target from unresponsive-target) at the moment of timeout — and expose a content-free summary for logs that must not carry user data, verified by a test.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/wait.rs`: *"A timed-out wait carries `WaitDiagnostics` describing what was on screen when it gave up, so the caller never needs a follow-up call to find out why. The 2026-07-24 tabbed-AskUserQuestion bug had to be diagnosed by driving a stuck session key-by-key over the bridge; that evidence is now captured at the moment of failure."* The `ended` field *"distinguishes 'we typed into a dead PTY' from 'the TUI ignored us', which previously both surfaced as a bare AUTO_FAILED."* Privacy split: `shape()` renders `screen=1841ch · gen=… · state=… · ended=…` for the shareable debug log; full text goes only to `tracing` behind `PERSONAS_FLEET_DEBUG`. The redaction contract is enforced by test `shape_is_content_free` asserting the shape never contains screen content. Diagnostics are built only on a miss, "so a successful wait costs no screen render."

observed.title: Actively strip inherited environment when spawning nested agent CLIs — not setting it isn't enough
observed.statement: A child CLI spawned from a process that was itself launched by that CLI inherits identity/auth env markers that silently change the child's behaviour; maintain an explicit env_remove list for nesting markers and credential variables, shared by every spawn path.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/pty.rs` — two distinct strip lists, both applied via `cmd.env_remove`: (1) `CLAUDE_NESTING_ENV` (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, …): with markers present, Claude >=2.1.19x *"silently runs as a NESTED/child session: it never registers in ~/.claude/sessions and — critically — never persists a `<session-id>.jsonl` transcript, so Hibernate/Wake and orphan-Resume fail … Root-caused live 2026-07-02 via A/B console spawns: identical argv, markers present -> no session storage; markers stripped -> registers + persists."* (2) `CLI_SUBSCRIPTION_RESERVED_ENV` (API keys/base URLs): *"Not setting it isn't enough — if it's present, claude prompts 'Detected a custom API key… use it?' … and derails into a fresh OAuth login a headless fleet session can't complete."* Both lists are shared with the headless spawn path (`headless.rs` imports `CLAUDE_NESTING_ENV` from `pty`), so the fix cannot drift between lanes.

observed.title: Parse a stated reset time for one scheduled retry; refuse ambiguity and keep the blind cadence as fallback
observed.statement: When a rate-limit banner states its own reset time, parse it to schedule exactly ONE retry at reset+grace — but treat any parsing ambiguity as 'no ETA' (a wrong ETA silences retries until a moment that never comes), and fall back to the blind retry cadence after the scheduled attempt fires, in case the stated time didn't hold.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/stale.rs` — `parse_limit_reset()` + `limit_retry_pass()`. Inline decisions: the stated time is treated as local wall-clock (parsing the `(Europe/Prague)` parenthetical "would mean shipping a tz database for zero behavioural gain"); *"Ambiguity yields `None` … A wrong ETA is worse than no ETA: it would silence the retries until a moment that never comes"* — a bare `7:50` with no meridiem is refused, and a reset >24h out is treated as a misparse. `LIMIT_RESET_GRACE_MS = 2 min` because "Claude's clock and ours are not the same clock, and a retry that lands one second early just burns the attempt." The `fired_after_reset` flag guarantees the scheduled lane spends exactly one attempt, then reverts to the 4/15-min cadence capped at `LIMIT_RETRY_MAX = 24` sized to "a 5-hour session-limit window". The banner signature list is deliberately narrow ("sessions legitimately *talk about* rate limits, so bare 'rate limit' does not match") and was corrected from live evidence ("the first signature guess missed it and 8 of 16 sessions sat invisible").

observed.title: When lifecycle events and process ownership disagree, the owned process is authoritative
observed.statement: For entities backed by a live OS process, treat process death (the reaper) as the authoritative exit signal and demote protocol-level end events to advisory: ignore an 'ended' event while the child is demonstrably alive, and never let any later event downgrade a confirmed Exited state.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/hooks.rs` `apply_hook()`, the `sessionend` arm: *"The in-session `/resume` (and `/clear`) restart claude IN THE SAME PTY, firing SessionEnd for the OLD session id while the PTY child stays alive — verified live … Marking it Exited here would grey out a working session, and the 'don't downgrade Exited' guard just below would then pin it dead forever. For a PTY-owned session the reaper (actual process death) is authoritative, so ignore SessionEnd while the child is alive. External (hook-only) sessions have no child to reap, so SessionEnd stays their exit signal."* The complementary invariant right below: *"Don't downgrade an Exited session — process death is authoritative."* Division of labour: hooks carry *intent* signals, the transcript watcher carries *aliveness*, and the reaper alone carries death.

observed.title: Never render a corrupt or empty row as an actionable control — skip it loudly
observed.statement: When listing rows that become clickable consent/approval surfaces, a row with an unparseable payload or a blank action must be skipped with a warning, not defaulted — `unwrap_or_default()` turns garbage into an approvable no-op the user can consent to.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/companion/approvals/approval_lifecycle.rs` `companion_list_pending_approvals`: *"Skip corrupt/empty payloads instead of unwrap_or_default()-ing them into a card with a blank action — that rendered an *actionable* approval (the user can click Approve) whose action is \"\", a consent surface showing a no-op as if it were a real decision."* Both failure modes get a `tracing::warn!` with the approval id and `continue`. The same query also enforces a consent-freshness window in SQL (`created_at >= datetime('now', ?1)`): *"a pending approval older than this is stale and must not be presented as actionable."* The general rule: on a consent surface, fail-closed per row beats fail-soft defaults — a default is itself a fabricated decision.

observed.title: When deleting an approval allowlist, restate every surviving guard at the deletion site
observed.statement: If a consent gate is deliberately removed (e.g. 'autonomous mode IS the standing consent'), write the decision as a historical note at the removal site that enumerates each remaining bound by name and states plainly which previously-held-back actions now fire unattended — so the risk was accepted explicitly, not discovered later.
observed.detail_md: `src-tauri/src/commands/companion/approvals/approval_autopilot.rs` opens with a dated note ("2026-08-10 — operator's explicit call, risk accepted") recording that `AUTOAPPROVE_ALLOWLIST` is GONE, with the reasoning ("a mode whose whole promise is 'act without asking me' that then files a card for two thirds of what Athena proposes … is a slower manual mode with extra steps"), then a numbered list of what still bounds an auto-fire — the dispatcher's `ALLOWED_ACTIONS` capability boundary, `validate_fleet_cwd` confinement to registered project dirs, the boldness dial + screen re-check, per-executor gates, and the editable plan card — each flagged "none of it may be weakened." It closes with *"Two consequences worth stating plainly rather than discovering later"*: 30 backlog verdicts and externally-visible connector writes now fire without a click, and names the rollback ("Turning autonomous mode OFF is the way to get those clicks back"). ADR discipline embedded at the exact code site a future editor would touch.

observed.title: Pair a no-replay event with a consume-on-mount latch for lazy-mounted deep links
observed.statement: When a deep-link intent is emitted over a fire-and-forget bus toward a component that lazy-mounts, also record the intent in a single-slot module latch; the target consumes the latch on mount AND subscribes live, so the emit can never land before the subscriber exists.

observed.title: Persist only a filter's stable dimensions; reset absolute timestamps and drill-ins on restore
observed.statement: When persisting a view's filter state, save only the dimensions that stay meaningful across sessions (status/severity/source enums) and deliberately null out absolute timestamps and transient drill-in scopes on load, so the view never reopens into a stale or surprising deep-filter.

observed.title: Fire the inbox-zero celebration only when a user action drained it — arm a ref, judge after settle
observed.statement: Gate a 'you cleared it!' celebration on an armed ref set only by real user actions, evaluated after the refresh settles and only on the un-narrowed default view — so a filter change or background poll reaching zero can never trigger a false celebration.

observed.title: Collapse mixed backend detail blobs to prose-or-facts, bailing to prose on any ambiguity
observed.statement: Normalize a field that arrives in several shapes (free prose, key=value lists, JSON, raw error text) through tiered parsers into one predictable prose-or-facts union, where any parse ambiguity degrades to prose (nothing lost) and pretty JSON is preserved separately for a power-user 'show raw' affordance.
observed.detail_md:
`src/features/overview/sub_incidents/libs/incidentDetail.ts` normalizes `AuditIncident.detail`, which the Rust promoter fills with four different shapes, "so the inbox never renders a raw JSON / `key=value` blob at a non-technical user." Result type: `{ kind: 'empty'|'prose'|'facts', prose, facts, rawJson }`.

Two load-bearing details: (1) the key=value parser is strict per-part so a sentence containing `=` can't be shredded — `const KV_PART = /^\s*[\w.-]+\s*=\s*.+$/;` with `if (!KV_PART.test(part)) return null; // not a clean kv list — bail to prose`. (2) JSON that parses keeps `rawJson = JSON.stringify(parsed, null, 2)` alongside extracted facts, so the modal can offer raw view "without it leaking into the default reading path"; JSON that fails to parse returns null with the comment "expected for prose that merely starts with a brace." `normalizeIncidentDetail` never throws; the fallthrough order is JSON -> kv-list -> prose. Key humanization goes through an `ACRONYMS` table (`id -> ID`, `url -> URL`).

observed.title: Re-derive keep/delete from the user's resolution and assert they differ before a destructive apply
observed.statement: When a conflict pair's A/B slots can be reordered by the model layer, resolve the user's choice into explicit keep/remove rows at apply time, assert they are distinct, and mirror the backend's refusal rules (pinned tier, cross-owner merge) client-side for a clear message instead of a generic failure.

observed.title: Precompute pair features once and prune O(n²) comparisons with best-case bounds
observed.statement: In an all-pairs similarity scan, compute per-item features (token sets, bigram sets) once up front, drive multiple metrics from a single intersection pass, and skip the expensive metric whenever even its perfect score could not cross the decision threshold.

observed.title: Mirror the last good parse in memory so storage corruption degrades to session data, not loss
observed.statement: Back a localStorage-persisted collection with a module-level mirror of the last successful load, return the mirror on any read failure, and toast the corruption exactly once with copy that differs depending on whether the mirror could rescue anything.

observed.title: Union-merge partially-overlapping queries so the headline signal always renders its own row
observed.statement: When a panel joins two queries that have different limits and filters (so neither covers the other), merge by union and let the signal-side row render from its own fields when the primary list never loaded it — dropping it because the other page is short would rebuild the very bug the panel exists to expose.

observed.title: Make automated bypasses of a human queue visible, detected from the writer's stable markers
observed.statement: When a policy (trust_llm / auto-triage) resolves items without a human and there is no structured column recording that, detect it from the exact machine markers the backend writes into the notes field, render a visible badge with the machine's reasoning, and pin the producer's exact strings in tests naming the Rust source sites.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_manual-review/libs/reviewHelpers.ts` — `detectAutoResolution` closes the gap named in its doc: "Surfacing this closes the 'auto-send is a convention, not a visible invariant' gap (UAT P5 — F-NO-CONFIDENCE-AUTORESOLVE)." There is "no structured `auto_resolved` column, so these well-known substrings are the signal" — `\btrust_llm\b` and `\bauto_triage\b`, plus a reasoning extractor for the note shape `"auto_triage LLM verdict: Approve — <reasoning>"`. `components/AutoResolvedBadge.tsx` renders the badge so "the silent bypass of the human queue is no longer invisible in the UI." The cross-language contract is pinned in `libs/__tests__/reviewHelpers.test.ts`, whose header cites the producers by file: "The note strings below are the EXACT machine markers the Rust backend writes: engine/dispatch.rs -> trust_llm … engine/auto_triage.rs -> 'auto_triage LLM verdict: …'" — including the fallback note and a negative case ('does NOT flag a human-written note'). Prefer a structured column where possible; where prose is the only channel, this is the disciplined version: documented producers, anchored patterns, exact-string tests.

observed.title: When a panel re-scopes a shared store list, capture the prior query and re-issue it on unmount
observed.statement: A surface that narrows a shared store collection to a different bucket must snapshot the query the previous consumer was using on first render and re-issue it on unmount, or the surface it borrowed the store from is left filtering the wrong bucket and renders empty after close.

observed.title: Stamp a last-seen watermark on leaving the surface and derive 'N new since' client-side
observed.statement: Persist an ISO last-seen timestamp when the user leaves an inbox (unmount) rather than tracking per-row read flags, then derive the 'new since your last visit' count by comparing loaded rows against the watermark — with an explicit 'mark seen' action to reset it mid-visit.

observed.title: Anchor score charts to the metric's fixed scale, never the sample's min/max
observed.statement: When a score has a bounded scale (0-5, 0-100), project sparklines and distributions onto that fixed range rather than auto-scaling to the visible sample, so the same value sits at the same vertical position on every row and trends stay comparable across entities at a glance.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_director/directorScore.ts`: "The score scale is fixed (0-5), never min/max of the sample, so a '4' sits in the same vertical position everywhere — trends stay comparable across personas at a glance." `sparklinePoints` maps `y = h - pad - (s / SCORE_MAX) * (h - pad*2)`. Consumed by `ScoreSparkline.tsx` (per-row roster trend, with a faint baseline at score 0 and a tooltip carrying the actual numbers: "the line shows the shape, the tooltip shows the actual numbers") and the command-center distribution — one shared color/shape vocabulary module instead of per-surface chart code.

observed.title: Snapshot the id set before running a sequential batch of long operations
observed.statement: A batch action over a filtered/derived set (each item a minutes-long operation) must copy the ids at click time and iterate that frozen array sequentially with inline N-of-M progress — if the batch re-reads the live filtered list, a data refresh between items reshuffles or regrows the set mid-flight, skipping or double-processing items.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_director/useSequentialReview.ts`: "`run` snapshots the ids it's given, so a portfolio refresh between reviews can't reshuffle the set mid-flight." The hook is a 25-line primitive (`progress: number | null`, `running = progress !== null`, `for` loop awaiting `onReview(ids[i])`, `finally { setProgress(null) }`) shared by two header actions: `ReviewFilteredAction.tsx` ("Review these N" — runs the Director over exactly the agents the active facet filter narrowed to, "sequentially (each run is a real LLM pass)") and `StaleSweepButton.tsx` (one-click re-review of all >14d-stale agents, rendering nothing when none are stale). Both surface `loadingText` = done/total.

observed.title: Model a multi-surface facet filter as one discriminated union with toggle-to-clear
observed.statement: When several dashboard widgets (triage chips, histogram bands, momentum buckets, a table toggle) can each narrow the same list, model the active facet as a single discriminated-union value owned by the parent, with a payload-aware equality helper and a toggle helper where re-selecting the active facet clears it — every surface then renders its own pressed state and stays in sync for free.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_director/rosterFilter.ts`: `type RosterFilter = {type:'flagged'} | {type:'flag';flag} | {type:'score';score} | {type:'momentum';momentum}`; `sameFilter` compares type + payload; `toggleFilter(current,next) = sameFilter ? null : next`; `rosterRowMatches` is an exhaustive switch. "One facet is active at a time and any of four surfaces can drive it... The state lives in DirectorCoachingTab so all of them stay in sync." Driving surfaces: `AttentionTriageBar.tsx`, `ScoreDistribution.tsx`, `MomentumSummary.tsx`, `PersonaCoachingTable.tsx` — each calls `onSelect(toggleFilter(filter, {...}))` and sets `aria-pressed`.

observed.title: Reading only allSettled's fulfilled branch makes persistent failure look fresh
observed.statement: When a dashboard fans out to N sources with Promise.allSettled and only consumes the fulfilled branches, a permanently failing source degrades to silent stale/'unknown' rows indistinguishable from healthy data. Give each source its own error slot, and route them through the existing combined error channel so the current banner fires on partial failure without any consumer change.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_health/libs/useStatusPageData.ts`: "a rejected SLA or healing fetch previously vanished (Promise.allSettled only read the `fulfilled` branch), leaving `error` null and every persona rendering as a silent stale/'unknown' entry with no indication anything failed." Fix: `slaError` / `healingError` state per source, `combinedError = error ?? slaError ?? healingError` ("so the existing InlineErrorBanner picks them up without any consumer change") plus individual exposure for attribution. Same doctrine backend-side: `src/api/overview/health.ts` health bundle — "Each source is independently fail-able via `bundle.errors`, so one failing query degrades a single source instead of nuking the whole view", surfaced by `HeartbeatsView.tsx`'s `StalenessBanner` naming the failed sources.

observed.title: Build filter vocabularies from a registry unioned with observed rows
observed.statement: A type/category filter over an event stream should offer the union of a server-side known-vocabulary registry (curated seed plus every type ever observed) and the types present in currently loaded rows — the registry lets users filter for a type before any matching row has loaded, and loaded rows backfill brand-new types the registry hasn't refreshed yet.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_events/libs/useEventLog.ts` `availableTypes`: "The registry is the primary source (so a listener can be filtered for even before any matching event has loaded); loaded rows backfill any type not yet in the registry." Backed by `src/api/overview/events.ts` `listKnownEventTypes` — "the curated builtin seed merged with every distinct type observed in `persona_events`. Feeds the events type filter and trigger/listener creation so discovery isn't limited to loaded rows." Both fetches are best-effort: "the type filter still works from loaded rows if these fail." A companion `getEventSkippedStats` surfaces the no-subscriber rate as a dead/misrouted-trigger signal.

observed.title: Parse timestamps to epoch before comparing when the backend mixes formats
observed.statement: Never sort or cursor-compare timestamp strings lexicographically when the producer can emit more than one shape (RFC3339 'T...Z' vs SQLite-naive 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') — a string compare misorders the moment the two mix. Parse to epoch ms once, guard NaN, and pick the true oldest for pagination cursors regardless of display sort direction.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_events/libs/useEventLog.ts` `loadOlder`: "Pick the chronologically oldest event regardless of sort direction. Compare parsed epoch ms, not raw strings — the backend emits both RFC3339 ('...T...Z') and SQLite-naive ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') shapes, and a lexicographic compare misorders them if the two ever mix." The loop tracks `oldestMs` with `Number.isNaN` guards, and newly fetched pages are additionally filtered to `ms < oldestMs` after id-dedupe so a server that ignores the `until` cursor can't loop the pagination. The row sort in `filteredEvents` likewise pre-parses all `created_at` into a `tsMap` before sorting.

observed.title: Ship the client's UTC offset with every day-bucketed query
observed.statement: Any backend aggregation that buckets by 'day' (SLA trends, health windows, daily uptime) should receive the caller's UTC offset (`-new Date().getTimezoneOffset()`) as a standard parameter so days align with the user's local calendar — otherwise a persona that fails every evening local time smears across two UTC days and the trend lies.
observed.detail_md: `src/api/overview/sla.ts`: `const localUtcOffsetMinutes = () => -new Date().getTimezoneOffset();` passed as `utcOffsetMinutes` to `get_sla_dashboard` — "so the backend buckets the trend and the window by the user's local day." Same convention in `src/api/overview/health.ts` `getHealthBundle` (`utcOffsetMinutes: -new Date().getTimezoneOffset()`). The convention is applied at the API-seam wrapper, so no call site can forget it.

observed.title: Lazy-gate an optional module's fetch cluster on its anchor entity — but explicit routes must still resolve ready
observed.statement: When an optional feature (not seeded on every install/tier) has both an always-mounted teaser and an explicitly navigated page sharing one data hook, give the hook a `lazy` option: teaser callers wait for the feature's anchor entity to be confirmed present (derived from already-loaded state, no extra IPC) before firing the fetch cluster; the explicit route stays eager because it must resolve `ready` even when the anchor is absent, so it renders an empty state instead of hanging on a spinner forever.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_director/useDirector.ts`: `lazy` option — "For surfaces that mount unconditionally alongside other content (e.g. the personas-page teaser)... avoids firing the cluster on every page load when Director isn't seeded for this install/tier. Default `false` preserves the original eager-fetch-on-mount behavior for surfaces (the Director command-center tab) that need `ready` to resolve even when `director` turns out to be absent, so they can render their own empty state instead of hanging on a spinner forever." Gate: `if (lazy && !director) return; refresh();` where `director` derives from the agent store's personas (`trust_origin === 'system' && name === 'Director'`) with no extra IPC. The hook is the single source for both surfaces ("instead of each re-implementing the same Promise.all fetch").

observed.title: Pin code-config to locale-catalog parity with a key-set equality test
observed.statement: When a code map is the single source of truth for both a visual attribute and an i18n token key (verdict -> accent + token), add a unit test asserting the map's token-key set equals the catalog section's key set exactly — a value added to one side but not the other then fails CI instead of degrading silently to an unstyled fallback badge or a raw untranslated token.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_certification/components/VerdictBadge.tsx`: `VERDICT_CONFIG` unifies what were "two independently hand-maintained literal maps... a new verdict added to one but not the other degraded silently (unstyled `slate` badge, or a raw un-translated token rendered to the user)." `__tests__/VerdictBadge.test.tsx` imports `en.json` directly and asserts `Object.values(VERDICT_CONFIG).map(c => c.tokenKey).sort()` equals `Object.keys(en.status_tokens.verdict).sort()`, plus a rendered-label check and a slate-fallback check for unrecognized verdicts (which still derive a lowercased token key rather than crashing).

observed.title: Cap an LLM survey by territory, not by item count
observed.statement: A 'return at most N high-signal items' brief over a large corpus is satisfiable without doing the survey — the agent mines the cheapest ground, hits the cap, and stops. Bound the work by assigning each session ONE named territory (with its file paths and last-visited date) and remove the item cap entirely; volume is then bounded by what the territory genuinely contains, and machine guards (max items per ingest, max payload bytes) catch runaways.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_patterns/practiceHarvestPrompt.ts` lines 14-23: "The first engine sent ONE agent at a whole repository with a ~15-item cap … a measured run spent ~11 tool calls over 8,568 files, returned 14 items, and every single one came from a root config file … The agent was complying, not failing." The fix: `scopeSection()` gives each session one scope id + its `paths`, and `BUDGET` states "there is no cap … The ingest door caps a single run at 120 candidates (MAX_INGEST_PER_RUN) and 1 MiB of JSON — those are the machine guards. A prompt-level cap does not improve quality, it just stops the reading early." The scope section also forbids harvesting root configs from a non-global scope: "this is the single most common way a harvest fakes coverage."

observed.title: Close every author-chosen metadata axis, and delete the axis that cannot discriminate
observed.statement: When many agents (or people) author metadata, an axis left as a prompt suggestion fragments into noise, and an axis whose instructions predetermine its answer returns one value forever. Ship each classification axis as a closed vocabulary from the single enforcing source, quarantine unknown values on an 'unsorted' shelf, and delete axes that measurements show cannot discriminate.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_patterns/practiceHarvestPrompt.ts` lines 107-115: the free-text `ftype` axis "produced NINETY distinct values across 330 items … while the enforced `topic` axis held at 5.8 items/topic. A filter over a field where every writer coins their own value is not a filter." And: "`durability` is gone from the contract entirely: the same scan returned `durable` for 330 of 330 items, because this prompt tells authors mechanical items don't belong here, so the axis can never discriminate." The topic vocabulary itself lives in ONE place (Rust `db/repos/workspace_taxonomy.rs`, shipped inside snapshot.json) "so there is exactly one copy of it and this prompt cannot drift from what the ingest door enforces" (lines 66-71). `libraryPulse.ts::isWellFormedTopic` scores structural conformance as a health pillar.

observed.title: Detect a dispatched CLI session's completion as leaving the active states, never as process exit
observed.statement: An interactive CLI session that finished its work sits at 'idle' (the prompt) forever — it never reaches 'exited'. Auto-ingest of dispatched work must fire on the transition out of a set of ACTIVE states (spawning/running/awaiting_input), track liveness per dispatch key, prefix-match fan-out session names (key plus ':scope' suffixes), and seed the just-dispatched key as live so a fast-settling session still produces a live-to-gone transition even if the first poll misses it.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_patterns/useHarvestAutoIngest.ts`: header comment — "'Ends' means settling out of the active states — for an interactive CLI session that is `idle` (the prompt), NOT `exited`: a finished session sits idle forever (live-test finding, 2026-07-23)." `const ACTIVE = new Set(['spawning','running','awaiting_input'])`; `markLive()` pre-seeds `wasLive` at dispatch; the poll matches `s.name === key || s.name.startsWith(key + ':')` because after scope fan-out "matching session names exactly … would silently never fire again, since no session carries the bare key." Ingest is idempotent via a run-dir `ingested.json` marker, so firing on idle/exit/vanish is safe; an in-flight `ingesting` Set prevents double fire.

observed.title: Give human adjudication its own timestamp, distinct from the row's updatedAt
observed.statement: Any surface that windows on 'what was decided lately' must key on a dedicated decidedAt column set only when a human adjudicates, never on updatedAt — background maintenance (re-verification, taxonomy renormalization) touches updatedAt and would resurface months-old decisions as this week's news.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_patterns/libraryModel.ts` lines 36-40 on `KnowledgeItemView.decidedAt`: "When a human adjudicated it (adopt/reject/deprecate); null while pending. The digest windows on this, not `updatedAt` — a re-verification or a topic renormalization touches `updatedAt` and would otherwise resurface months-old decisions as 'this week'." Consumed by `libraryPulse.ts::computeDigest`, which filters `isAfter(i.decidedAt, cutoff)` for adopted/rejected/deprecated buckets while machine-harvested arrivals key on `createdAt` — three timestamps, three distinct meanings.

observed.title: Weight aggregate read-depth by territory size, and return null over an empty denominator
observed.statement: When rolling per-scope coverage into one number, done/total alone lets a corpus skimmed at 11% look finished. Compute the depth figure as a file-count-weighted mean of per-scope read percentages (100% of 100 files must not cancel 10% of 900), exclude scopes that reported no depth rather than assuming them complete, and return null — not 0/0 — when there is nothing to report so the UI stays silent instead of implying 'nothing to do here'.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_patterns/harvestWave.ts::coverageRatio`: "a scope skimmed at 11% and one read exhaustively both count as 'harvested'. `pct` is the file-weighted mean read-depth … a repo that has been visited everywhere and read nowhere cannot look finished." Weighting loop: `const w = Math.max(1, Number(r.fileCount)); weighted += pct * w`. Pinned in `__tests__/harvestWave.test.ts`: "weights read-depth by territory size, not by scope count — 100% of a small territory must not cancel out 10% of a large one" (900-file@10% + 100-file@100% -> 19, not 55); and "counts a harvested scope by its timestamp, not by its yield" — read-and-found-nothing is covered.

observed.title: Match a rate's numerator and denominator to the same population and window
observed.statement: A rate computed from mismatched populations lies confidently. Two concrete traps: dividing failures by ALL executions (including running/queued/cancelled) inflates the denominator so error_rate + success_rate no longer sum to 100 and alerts under-fire; and using a lifetime issue tally as the numerator over a windowed execution count marks a currently-healthy worker as failing. Fix by pinning both sides: decided runs only in the denominator, currently-open failures only in the numerator.
observed.detail_md: Two sites. `src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts::evaluateRule` lines 55-70: "error_rate / success_rate use the DECIDED denominator — completed runs only … Dividing by totalExecutions (COUNT(*) over ALL statuses incl. running, queued, cancelled) inflated the denominator, so an error_rate rule could sit under its threshold while the SLA card showed a higher rate, and success_rate + error_rate failed to sum to 100%." `src/features/overview/libs/fleetOptimizer.ts` lines 115-127: "counting [resolved issues] tanked the success rate of a persona that runs fine today (e.g. 12 long-resolved issues + 20 windowed execs => a false 40% rate => a wrong 'High Cost, Low Success')" — fixed to `Math.min(healing.open, totalExecs)`.

observed.title: Never ship a hardcoded constant that renders as a computed metric — measure it, with a minimum-sample floor
observed.statement: A literal like strength: 0.7 displayed on an analytics edge reads as measurement and poisons trust in everything beside it. Replace it with the real computation (here: Jaccard overlap of two series' failure days over their shared window) and give the measurement a minimum-sample floor that returns 0 for 'too little shared history' — one coincident bad day must not print a 1.0 correlation.
observed.detail_md: `src/stores/slices/overview/personaHealthSlice.ts`: `CascadeLink.strength` doc — "Previously a hardcoded `0.7` that rendered as a computed-looking number but was never computed." Now `coFailureStrength()` computes |both failed| / |either failed| over shared active days, with `COFAIL_MIN_SAMPLE = 2`: "Below the floor, strength is 0 (insufficient shared history) rather than a noisy 1.0 from a single coincident bad day." The threshold `COFAIL_RATE_THRESHOLD = 0.70` deliberately matches the status-page day bands (`dayStatusFromRate`) so 'failure day' means the same thing everywhere. Exported for unit tests (`cascadeStrength.test.ts`).

observed.title: Retry only the failed sources of an aggregate bundle once before raising a staleness banner
observed.statement: When one server-side bundle replaces N independent fetches, keep each source independently fail-able (per-source error map in the response), then — before surfacing any degraded-data banner — run ONE automatic retry of only the failed sources through their individual endpoints. This absorbs cold-start races (first bundle call landing before a session token is ready) without hammering healthy sources, and the banner that finally shows carries each source's concrete failure reason.
observed.detail_md: `src/stores/slices/overview/personaHealthSlice.ts::computePersonaHealth`: `getHealthBundle(7)` returns `bundle.errors` per source ("a single failing query no longer nukes the whole health view"); then "ONE automatic retry of ONLY the failed sources (via their individual endpoints) before we ever raise a staleness banner. Covers the cold-start IPC-token race where the first bundle call lands before the session token is ready" — `Promise.allSettled(failedNames.map(...))` with a switch to per-source endpoints, clearing `reasons[name]` on success. `DataSourceStatus.reason` carries "*why* a source is unavailable, not just *that* it is." Sources with a graceful fallback (per-persona stats -> labeled fleet proxy) are deliberately NOT part of the retry/banner surface.

observed.title: When two evaluators can fire the same rule, share cooldown through the persisted fire log
observed.statement: A client-side alert loop plus a backend evaluator (running even with the UI closed) will double-fire the same rule unless their dedup state is shared. Make the persisted fired-alerts log the shared cooldown authority: the client force-refreshes history every tick (bypassing its TTL) so it sees backend fires, falls back from its in-memory cooldown map to the last persisted fire (so a reload doesn't instantly re-fire a still-triggering rule), and guards its own tick with a running flag so a slow pass can't overlap the next one and race past the cooldown check.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useGlobalAlertEvaluator.ts`: "history is force-fetched each tick: the Rust alert evaluator (the NOC authority, running even with the UI closed) persists its fires to `fired_alerts`, and only a FRESH history read lets this client loop's cooldown fallback see them — otherwise both loops could fire the same rule inside the TTL window (double toast + double incident)"; `if (running) return` overlap guard. `src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts` lines 389-399: "prefer the in-memory timestamp, but fall back to the most recent PERSISTED fired alert for this rule. The in-memory map resets on reload, so without this every still-triggering rule re-fired immediately after a restart." Failed persists go into `pendingSyncAlertIds` and are retried next cycle.

observed.title: Age-gate 'live' alerts derived from a retained analytics window
observed.statement: Dashboards retain anomalies across their whole window, so a recommendation engine that surfaces any above-threshold anomaly renders a weeks-old spike as a current critical. Add an explicit recency bound (a few days) on top of the magnitude threshold before an event may masquerade as happening now; older anomalies stay visible in history, not in the 'act on this' slot.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/libs/fleetOptimizer.ts` lines 64-70: "The dashboard retains anomalies across its whole window, so without a recency bound a weeks-old spike renders as a current critical. A live, actionable spike is one from the last few days" — `ANOMALY_RECENCY_DAYS = 3` filters `dashboard.cost_anomalies` alongside the `deviation_sigma >= 2.0` magnitude gate, with a NaN-safe date parse.

observed.title: Take pointer capture only after drag slop, and swallow the trailing click
observed.statement: On a pannable canvas with clickable nodes, capturing the pointer on pointerdown retargets the entire pointer stream — including the eventual click — at the canvas, so node clicks never fire and every tap reads as background. Capture only once movement exceeds a small slop (~3px), and after a real pan ends set a one-shot flag consumed in a capture-phase click handler so releasing a drag over a node doesn't select it. Any manual gesture also cancels an in-flight animated camera move — the user always wins the camera.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_patterns/graph/useGraphCanvas.ts` lines 106-150: "Pointer capture is taken ONLY once a real pan starts (past the slop): capturing on pointerdown retargets the whole pointer stream — including the eventual click — at the svg, so node clicks never fired and every tap read as 'background'. After a pan ends, the trailing click is suppressed." Mechanism: `drag.moved` slop check -> `setPointerCapture` on first real move; `suppressClick` ref consumed in `onClickCapture` with `stopPropagation + preventDefault`. `onPointerDown`/wheel/`zoomBy` all call `cancelFlight()` (flyTo animation): "Any manual pan/wheel cancels it (the user always wins the camera)."

observed.title: Bind wheel-zoom as a native non-passive listener on the drawing element, not its container
observed.statement: Two documented failure modes in one listener choice: React's synthetic onWheel is passive by default, so a zoom that cannot preventDefault scrolls the page underneath on every notch — it must be a native addEventListener('wheel', fn, { passive: false }). And it must live on the SVG itself, not the wrapping container: overlays (modals, side rails) are DOM children of the container and wheel bubbling follows the DOM, so a container-level listener turns every scroll inside an overlay into a canvas zoom.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_patterns/graph/useGraphCanvas.ts` lines 82-105: "Wheel must be a native non-passive listener: React's synthetic onWheel is passive by default, and a zoom that cannot preventDefault scrolls the Overview page underneath the canvas on every notch. It lives on the SVG, not the container — the cluster modal and the playbooks rail are DOM children of the container, and bubbling follows the DOM, so a container listener turned every scroll inside an overlay into a canvas zoom." Zoom anchors the world point under the cursor: `x: cx - (cx - c.x) * s`. Companion techniques in the same file: `labelScale(k) = k^-0.62` counter-scaling keeps labels readable at 0.3x and non-billboard at 3x, and `lod()` opacity ramps gate detail by zoom.

observed.title: Zero-fill every date-by-series cell when pivoting long rows for stacked charts
observed.statement: Pivoting a long-format time series (one row per date x series) into wide rows for a stacked area/bar chart must zero-fill every missing (date, series) cell after collecting the full series set — a key absent from one row renders as undefined, which produces NaN tooltips and visual jumps in stacked geometry. Sum duplicates for the same cell rather than overwriting, and sort dates ascending on the way out.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_usage/libs/pivotToolUsage.ts::pivotToolUsageOverTime`: collects `allToolNames` first, then "Zero-fill: ensure every date has an entry for every tool so Recharts stacked AreaChart never sees undefined keys (which cause NaN tooltips and visual jumps)"; duplicates summed via `entry[name] = (entry[name] || 0) + row.invocations`. Sibling module `periodComparison.ts::mergePreviousPeriod` shows the companion move for ghost prev-period lines: fetch days*2, split at `points.length - periodDays`, and merge `prev_<key>` fields onto current rows by ordinal index, skipping non-numeric values.

observed.title: Audit a curated collection's members against live canon status, and suggest — never auto-apply — replacements
observed.statement: A curated collection (playbook, checklist, template) is a promise that following it applies current doctrine, so a member whose source item was deprecated, rejected, or deleted is worse than a missing one — it actively teaches something the organization abandoned. Compute staleness as a pure derived view (only 'adopted' counts as live), resolve a likely replacement through explicit relationship edges with a precedence (supersedes beats governs-parent), and surface both to the curator: which phase a replacement belongs in is judgement the system cannot make.
observed.detail_md: `src/features/overview/sub_patterns/graph/graphModel.ts::playbookStaleMembers` (lines 459-497): "a member whose pattern was deprecated, rejected or deleted is worse than a missing one — it teaches something the workspace has since abandoned. Only `adopted` patterns count as live."
