Replacement resolution: "`supersedes` is the explicit replacement; `governs` is the fallback" — supersedes short-circuits, governs only fills if nothing better. The additive twin `playbookSuggestedAdditions` proposes adopted patterns that `extends` a member, inheriting the parent's phase and slotting after it — "adding stays a curator click, never automatic." Both are pure functions over rows + edges, pinned by `__tests__/playbookIntegrity.test.ts` and `suggestedAdditions.test.ts`.

observed.title: Log the intents your matcher could NOT serve, and surface them to the curator
observed.statement: A routing/matching layer over a curated catalog (playbooks, templates, FAQ answers) should persist every unmatched request alongside per-entry match counts — the unmatched list is real-demand evidence of which situation has no catalog entry yet, sourced from actual requests rather than a curator's guess.

observed.title: Stamp the scope baseline once at activation and derive scope creep from it server-side
observed.statement: For any milestone/iteration cut, stamp a cut_at timestamp exactly once when the cut is activated, and derive 'added after cut' per member on the backend from membership time vs the stamp — scope creep then becomes a queryable fact instead of a retrospective argument, and no client can forget to mark it.
observed.detail_md:
`src/api/devTools/milestones.ts`:

```ts
/** Patch-style update. Setting status to 'active' stamps cut_at (once — the
 *  scope-creep baseline); 'shipped' stamps shipped_at. */
```

and on `setMilestoneItem`: "Upsert a scope member (add or re-bucket). `added_after_cut` derives on the backend: a new membership on an already-cut milestone is scope creep." The client never sets either flag; the backend owns both the once-only stamp and the derivation, so the creep signal is tamper-proof by construction. The same module also keeps rating semantics honest ("A `rating` is 1..5; `null` means UNRATED, which is not the same judgement as a 1").

observed.title: Cap a TTL cache's entry count — TTL gates freshness, not retention
observed.statement: A stale-while-revalidate cache needs a hard size cap with insertion-order eviction on top of its TTL: TTL only decides when data is stale, never when memory is released, so variadic keys (per-entity ids) grow forever in a long-lived session. Re-set a key on write so Map insertion order approximates LRU.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/staleWhileRevalidate.ts:21-37` — `MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES = 500` with the comment "TTL only gates freshness, not retention — without a size cap, a long-lived desktop session accumulates one entry per distinct key forever when keys are derived from anything variadic (per-persona/per-execution ids)". `_cache.delete(key); _cache.set(key, …)` on write refreshes insertion order (`:79-83`), and `evictOldestIfOverCap()` walks `Map.keys()` in insertion order.

observed.title: Drive N springs from one module rAF engine that writes to DOM refs
observed.statement: Instead of N independent framer-motion springs each firing setState at 60fps, register every animated number with one module-scoped rAF loop that integrates spring physics and writes straight to the DOM via a callback — zero React reconciliation per frame. Cap dt (~64ms) so a background-tab return doesn't produce a huge integration jump, and stop the loop when everything settles.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/rafAnimationEngine.ts` — one `tick` over a `Map<symbol, AnimationEntry>`, `dt = Math.min((now-last)/1000, 0.064)` "to avoid huge jumps after tab-switch", loop self-stops when `!anyActive`. Consumer `src/features/shared/components/display/AnimatedCounter.tsx:44-70` subscribes and only calls setState when the *formatted string* changes ("≈ once per integer crossing"), so React cost is proportional to visible change, not frames.

observed.title: Never classify infrastructure 'not found' by substring — anchor the exact shape
observed.statement: Deciding "this IPC command isn't registered" via `msg.includes('not found')` silently swallows every business not-found error ('project not found', 'host not found') into an empty-list fallback. Match the transport's canonical error shape with an anchored regex, or better, a structured `kind` field; real resource-not-found errors must propagate.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/tauri/safeInvoke.ts:17-53` documents the 2026-05-02 Wave 5 bug verbatim: two copies of the check existed, the `includes("not found")` copy coerced genuine backend errors into "command missing, return fallback", "producing empty-list UIs (e.g. '0 contexts') when the backend was genuinely erroring". The fix: `/^Command [^"]*"[\w_]+"[^"]* not found(?:\.|$)/i` anchored at start, plus structured `kind === 'not_found'` fast path. `safeInvoke(fallback, …)` re-throws everything else.

observed.title: Normalize unzoned SQLite datetimes to explicit UTC before Date parsing
observed.statement: SQLite's datetime('now') emits "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" — UTC with NO timezone marker — which `new Date()` misreads as LOCAL time, so a row written now displays as "2h ago" to a UTC+2 viewer. Detect the bare shape and append 'Z' at one chokepoint every timestamp formatter shares; pass through anything already zoned.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/formatters.ts:5-15` — `normalizeTimestamp` regex-detects bare `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS(.f)` and rewrites to `…T…Z`; every downstream formatter (`formatTimestamp`, `formatRelativeTime`) routes through it. The comment records the concrete symptom ("a row written 'now' can read '2h ago' for a UTC+2 viewer").

observed.title: Cache Intl.NumberFormat instances keyed by the options you actually vary
observed.statement: Intl.NumberFormat construction is one of the most expensive stdlib constructors (locale resolution + option validation) and formatters run on hot paths (per-rAF counters, dozens of table cells per pass). Instances are immutable and reusable — cache them in a module Map keyed by locale + the handful of option fields you vary; the cache is naturally bounded.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/formatters.ts:71-91` — module `numberFormatCache` keyed `locale|style|currency|notation|minFrac|maxFrac`, with the comment noting `<AnimatedCounter>` invokes its formatFn on every rAF tick. All of formatCost/formatPercent/formatCount/formatCompactNumber share it.

observed.title: Classify errors structured-kind-first with regex fallback, into transient/permanent plus retry hints
observed.statement: Give the client one classifier that prefers the backend's structured error `kind` (no regex when the server already computed the taxonomy) and only falls back to message-pattern matching for foreign errors. Output a typed error carrying severity (transient/permanent/unknown) AND a suggested retryAfterMs, so retry policy lives with classification instead of being re-decided per call site.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/apiError.ts` — `classifyError` fast-paths `isTauriError(err)` through `TRANSIENT_KINDS`/`PERMANENT_KINDS` sets, regex tables only as fallback; `ApiError` carries `severity`, `retryAfterMs` (5000 for rate-limit, 2000 default, 0 for permanent), and the original `kind`. `withRetry` retries exactly once, only when `isTransient && retryAfterMs > 0`. The mirror type `src/lib/types/tauriError.ts` types the optional backend-computed `category`/`auto_fixable` fields as forward/backward-compatible.

observed.title: Detect silent key rotation by re-fetching the cheap PEM and re-importing only on change
observed.statement: When a frontend caches an imported public key whose backend keypair can rotate without the frontend restarting, don't trust the cache and don't re-import blindly: on an interval, refetch the cheap raw PEM, compare strings, and only pay the heavy CryptoKey import when the PEM actually changed. Share one in-flight refresh promise so concurrent encrypts during the stale window don't fan out, and clear the cache on any explicit invalidation event (logout).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/platform/crypto.ts:7-76` — documents the failure this defends against: "a stale cachedPublicKey would silently encrypt with an abandoned RSA key and the backend's decrypt would fail with an error indistinguishable from a transient IPC fault" (rotation causes: window reload, vault re-key, panic recovery, keyring fallback). 60s refresh interval, `pem === cachedPem` short-circuit, `refreshInFlight` dedupe, `clearCryptoCache()` on logout.

observed.title: Shield URLs behind placeholders before running path-redaction regexes
observed.statement: In a redaction pipeline, a filesystem-path regex will shred ordinary URLs — the `//host/path` portion matches the unix-path branch and destroys the URL before host/email rules ever see it. Match and protect full URLs first (swap in placeholder tokens, strip only query/fragment where secrets live), run the destructive passes, then restore. Redaction pass ORDER is part of the contract.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/sanitizers/maskSensitive.ts:53-68` — `FILE_PATH_RE` requires the leading `/` not be preceded by `:` or `/` "otherwise it also matches the //host/path portion of an ordinary URL … shredding it into `https:[path]` before EMAIL/host rules ever see it"; `URL_RE` is "matched and protected before FILE_PATH_RE runs", with `@@SANITIZED_URL_n@@` placeholders.

observed.title: Check hostile-input codepoints on the RAW string, before trim
observed.statement: JavaScript's trim() strips BOM and some zero-width characters — exactly the codepoints attackers use to disguise a `javascript:` scheme or hide a destination behind a bidi override. If you trim before scanning for unsafe codepoints, the evidence is destroyed and the check passes. Scan the original input first, then trim, then parse.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/sanitizers/sanitizeUrl.ts:93-99` — `sanitizeExternalUrl` comments "Check original input BEFORE trim — JS trim() strips BOM and some zero-width chars, which would let them slip past the check." The same ordering is deliberately mirrored in `src/lib/utils/sanitizers/variableSanitizer.ts:55-62` ("mirrors sanitizeUrl.ts's sanitizeExternalUrl ordering"), and `hasUnsafeCodepoints` enumerates C0/C1, ZWJ, LRM/RLM, bidi embedding/override/isolate ranges, BOM.

observed.title: Truncate at the type-appropriate limit BEFORE type dispatch, or big payloads corrupt silently
observed.statement: A sanitizer that applies a generic length slice up front and a larger type-specific cap later has already destroyed the data: the early 2000-char slice cut large JSON mid-structure — embedding malformed JSON into the prompt — and the later per-type re-slice was a no-op. Resolve the limit from the declared type first, then truncate once.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/sanitizers/variableSanitizer.ts:271-277` — `clean.slice(0, type === 'json' ? MAX_JSON_VALUE_LENGTH : MAX_VALUE_LENGTH)` with the inline post-mortem: "applying the generic 2000-char slice up front silently cut large JSON mid-structure … because the later `case 'json'` re-slice was then a no-op."

observed.title: Pause toast lifetimes on hover AND on tab-background, re-anchoring the clock on resume
observed.statement: A toast's auto-dismiss timer must pause while hovered and while the document is hidden (or timers silently burn through their duration off-screen), and resuming must re-anchor the tick clock to now so the paused interval is never counted as elapsed. Keep the visible progress bar CSS-driven (animation + a data-paused attribute + a --duration custom property) so pause/resume stays smooth; JS owns only the dismiss decision and the label.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/chrome/useToastTimer.ts` — `isPaused = paused || !isDocumentVisible`; `onMouseLeave` comment: "Drift correction: resuming after a hover pause must not count the paused interval as elapsed time, so re-anchor the tick clock to 'now'". Progress bar in `ToastContainer.tsx:127-140` is `animate-toast-progress` with `data-paused` and `style={{'--toast-duration': …}}`.

observed.title: Cap every ambient indicator set and collapse the excess into one +N counter
observed.statement: Any unbounded ambient surface — toast stacks, orbiting activity dots, capacity strips — needs a visible-count cap with the overflow collapsed into a single "+N" element, so the chrome stays legible under load and the user still knows the total. Sort by priority before slicing so the cap drops the least important items.
observed.detail_md: Evidence ×3: `src/features/shared/chrome/ToastContainer.tsx:241-275` — sort by priority desc then timestamp, `slice(0, MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS)`, overflow chip rendered via the same AnimatePresence; `src/features/shared/chrome/sidebar/OrbitDots.tsx:23,62-67,116-128` — `MAX_VISIBLE_DOTS = 6`, last arc slot becomes a `+N` counter so "the arc stays tight around the button"; `src/features/shared/chrome/fleetStripModel.ts:100-108` — running/queued cells clamp to the slot count.

observed.title: Every badge owns its own poll registration — never ride another surface's ticker
observed.statement: A count badge that stays fresh only because some OTHER component happens to poll the same store is a latent bug: collapse that component and the badge freezes at a stale number. Register the badge's own refresh on the shared polling coordinator's bucket (so it coalesces with everyone else's tick instead of adding a private setInterval on its own offset).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/chrome/useTitleBarTray.tsx:69-102` — "The tray never fetched anything: the review badge was only ever fresh because the SIDEBAR happened to poll pendingReviewCount on its own ticker, so a window with the sidebar collapsed showed a number that stopped moving. And the count it did read came from a raw setInterval living beside it, which ticked on its own offset and made SQLite warm its cache a second time for a badge." Fix: `getPollingCoordinator().register('titleBarPendingCounts', …, { interval: POLLING_CONFIG.dashboardRefresh.interval })`. A second registration for the dispatch badge documents why the two counts stay separate: decision queue vs execution queue — "Summing them would make one number that answers neither question."

observed.title: An aggregate badge must sum the authoritative total plus ONLY rowless terms — and pin the arithmetic in a test
observed.statement: Composing an "anything waiting on me?" number by hand-adding a subset of queues shows a confidently wrong 0 — worse than showing nothing. Take the backend's cross-queue total as the base, add client-side only the terms that genuinely have no backing row to count, never re-add a term the total already contains, and pin the arithmetic (including the double-count trap) in a dedicated test.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/chrome/useTitleBarTray.tsx:115-128` — the count "used to read questionCount + pendingReviewCount: two of SEVEN queues, so a reviewer with 26 pending ideas and nothing else saw 0. A confidently wrong number is worse than an absent one." Manual reviews are inside `pendingTotal` "and must NOT be added a second time"; build questions are the one client-side term because "a halted CLI awaiting input … has no row anywhere to count." The test `__tests__/useTitleBarTray.test.tsx:1-16` pins exactly this arithmetic and states "the double-count is the specific mistake this fix invites."

observed.title: Host background-service hooks in one lazy render-null component
observed.statement: Always-on background loops (event listeners, evaluators, reconcilers) import from heavy domain stores. Mount them all inside a single lazy-loaded component that renders null: the hook code and its ~hundreds of KB of store/API imports defer out of the main bundle and load after first paint, and the file doubles as the one inventory of every ambient loop the app runs, each with a comment saying why it exists.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/chrome/BackgroundServices.tsx` — header: "These hooks import from domain stores … which cascade ~300 KB of API + slice code. By lazy-loading this component, that code is deferred out of the main bundle and loaded after first paint. Renders nothing — purely a hook host." Eight background loops mounted, each with a rationale comment (alert evaluation "previously only fired while the Observability tab was open").

observed.title: Gate a restart-triggering action on live work and offer install-when-idle
observed.statement: An action that restarts the app (update install) silently kills in-flight jobs. Count live work before executing; if nonzero, interpose a three-way choice — proceed anyway / defer until idle / cancel — where "defer" is an effect that watches the running count and fires the action the moment it reaches zero, with a visible, cancellable pending state.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/chrome/UpdateBanner.tsx:17-53,120-163` — `runningCount` from active processes ("Installing restarts the app, which silently kills running runs — so warn before that happens"); `installWhenIdle` state + effect `if (installWhenIdle && runningCount === 0 && !isInstalling) { … installUpdate() }`; amber status band shows the deferral with a Cancel. Failed installs re-tone the banner red so "the user can see at a glance that the previous click didn't succeed."

observed.title: Smooth a live gauge with EMA plus two-threshold hysteresis in a pure DOM-free module
observed.statement: A polling gauge (CPU/RAM banding) flickers at threshold cusps unless you (a) damp samples with a small-alpha EMA, (b) use separate ENTER and EXIT thresholds per level so a metric must cross higher to worsen and fall lower to recover, and (c) never seed the smoother from a first sample the source marks invalid. Keep all tuning in a pure module so it's unit-testable with realistic traces, not point values.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/layout/systemLoad.ts` — `ema(prev, sample, alpha=0.25)`; ENTER/EXIT pairs per metric with "The gap between them is what stops the gauge flickering at a cusp"; worst-metric-wins, red held until BOTH metrics fall below red-exit. Consumer `src/features/shared/chrome/SystemLoadFooterIcon.tsx:62-71` skips seeding on `!m.sampleValid` ("CPU% not yet meaningful; don't seed the smoother off a 0") and pauses polling when the document is hidden. Trace-based test in `systemLoad.test.ts`.

observed.title: Bind semantic spacing tokens to density CSS variables so one setting reflows every card
observed.statement: Express card padding and section gaps as semantic tokens whose values are CSS custom properties set by an app-wide density setting (`p-[var(--density-pad)]`), with the default resolving to the historical values so appearance is unchanged out of the box. Deliberately exempt surfaces that should not breathe with density (modal chrome bands) and document the exemption on the token.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/utils/designTokens.ts:59-91` — `CARD_PADDING.standard = 'p-[var(--density-pad)]'`, `SECTION_GAP` via `--density-gap`/`--density-gap-lg`, comment: "flipping density reflows every card that uses these tokens … `modalSection` stays fixed — modal chrome bands should not breathe with content density." Same file's `STATE_LOCKED` records why locked cards use an overlay instead of opacity: "overlay approach avoids compounded opacity illegibility."

observed.title: Clamp the current page when row count changes — never reset to page 1
observed.statement: Resetting pagination to page 1 on every data-length change conflates a routine add/remove (deleting one row on page 4) with an actual filter change, yanking the user back to the start after ordinary edits. Keep the user's page and only pull it back when it falls out of range.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/DataGrid.tsx:163-174` — "Clamp (don't reset) the page when the row count changes. A plain reset to page 1 on every `data.length` change conflates routine add/remove (e.g. deleting a single row on page 4) with an actual filter change, which snapped the user back to page 1 after ordinary edits."

observed.title: Animate collapse height with grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr and gate overflow on transition settle
observed.statement: The CSS grid-row trick (`grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr` with a transition) animates height with zero DOM measurement and no per-frame layout pass, unlike animating `height`. If open content must escape clipping (nested dropdowns), reveal `overflow: visible` only via a settled flag set after the open transition completes — never while animating, or content spills mid-transition.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/Collapse.tsx:29-39,84-91` — "grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr with a transition gives a smooth height animation without measuring the DOM and without animating height, which forces a layout pass on every frame"; `settledOpen` is "True only once the open transition has settled; never while animating." Both directions pinned in `Collapse.test.tsx:62-88`. The component also reads prefers-reduced-motion itself because `<MotionConfig>` governs framer only, not CSS transitions.

observed.title: When a primitive replaces AnimatePresence, preserve unmount semantics and pin them in a test
observed.statement: A collapse/reveal primitive that keeps children mounted where the old code unmounted them silently leaves effects, subscriptions, and polling alive in every closed section. Offer explicit `unmountWhenClosed` semantics (keep mounted through the close transition, then drop; cancel the pending unmount on reopen) and write the regression test that states the stakes, because a mass migration multiplies the blast radius.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/Collapse.tsx:9-27,51-73` and `Collapse.test.tsx:5-11,45-52` — "81 of 86 migrated call sites previously unmounted their subtree … If `unmountWhenClosed` regressed to 'always mounted', every closed section in the app would keep its effects and subscriptions alive."

observed.title: Require a movement threshold before a resize handle commits a width
observed.statement: A drag-resize divider must ignore sub-threshold pointer movement (~3px) so a plain click never freezes a flexible `minmax(…,1fr)` column at its current pixel width, and must persist the width only if a real drag happened.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/ColumnResize.tsx:70-84` — "Ignore sub-threshold jitter so a plain click (vs. a deliberate drag) never freezes the column at its current width. `if (!drag.moved && Math.abs(delta) < 3) return;`" — localStorage persistence keyed by table id happens only after `drag.moved`.

observed.title: Under a global MotionConfig, must-run animations use CSS keyframes, not framer
observed.statement: An app-level `<MotionConfig reducedMotion={visible ? 'user' : 'always'}>` snaps EVERY framer animation (opacity included) when set to 'always' — silently killing reveals that must still play. Animations that must run regardless (or that need their own reduced-motion policy) belong in CSS keyframes, which MotionConfig does not govern; document the guard in the preset library so nobody reintroduces framer variants. When sequencing an ambient loop after an entrance, fill it `forwards` — `both` applies the loop's from-state during the start delay and fights the entrance.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/MotionizedGlyph.tsx:1-27` — "under `always` framer snaps EVERY animation (opacity included) — which silently killed the reveal"; the guard is re-documented in `motionPresets.ts:9-12`. Loop sequencing: `motionPresets.ts:156-164` — "The loop is 'forwards', NOT 'both': under 'both' its backwards fill would apply the from-state (a dimmed accent) during the start delay and fight the entrance", locked by `__tests__/MotionizedGlyph.test.tsx:87-105`.

observed.title: Replay a viewport-entry animation with IntersectionObserver plus a run key, skipping the first observation
observed.statement: To replay an entrance animation whenever an element re-enters the viewport without double-playing on mount, keep a `seen` ref that records the initial observation without firing, and bump a `runKey` (remounting the animated subtree) only on a genuine hidden→visible transition.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/MotionizedGlyph.tsx:102-120` — `if (seen.current === null) { seen.current = vis; return; } // initial observation` / `if (vis && !seen.current) setRunKey((k) => k + 1); // re-entered view → replay`.

observed.title: Guard display:contents wrappers against the 0×0 bounding rect
observed.statement: Chromium/WebView2 returns a zero rect from `getBoundingClientRect()` on a box-less (`display: contents`) wrapper, which pins anything positioned from it (tooltips, popovers) to the viewport's top-left. Detect the 0×0 rect and fall back to the wrapped child's real box.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/Tooltip.tsx:253-260` — `if (triggerRect.width === 0 && triggerRect.height === 0 && trigger.firstElementChild) { triggerRect = trigger.firstElementChild.getBoundingClientRect(); }`. Same file `:216-228` clears any already-scheduled show timer inside `show()` because a hover+focus pair could otherwise leave an orphaned timer firing after `hide()` — a ghost tooltip; and `:304-309` creates the portal only while the tooltip is actually shown ("a 250-node grid paid for 250 idle portals").

observed.title: Put aria-sort on the column-header element and swap the tag for grid faux tables
observed.statement: A sortable header primitive must place `aria-sort` on the element with the columnheader role — `<th>` implicitly, or an explicit `role="columnheader"` div for CSS-grid faux tables — and give the sort button a full next-action label. Verify every claim with tests, and lean on a global reduced-motion CSS reset instead of a per-component gate for the caret transition.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/SortableHeader.tsx:17-23,105-119` — "The column-header element carries aria-sort: `<th>` has an implicit columnheader role; the grid `<div>` gets an explicit one"; tests at `__tests__/SortableHeader.test.tsx:26-70`.

observed.title: Give shared primitives label FUNCTIONS, not translation keys
observed.statement: A domain-agnostic primitive stays i18n-free by accepting labels as functions — e.g. `summary: (group, count) => string` — so interpolation and the i18n import live in the (translated) caller. The primitive never learns about the catalog, and the pure model beneath it stays React-free and generic over row type via injected accessors.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/FacetedDecisionTable.tsx:9-13,23-36` — "Summary labels arrive as FUNCTIONS so interpolation stays in the (translated) caller — no i18n import lives in this file"; the model `facetedTableModel.ts:1-15` is dependency-free.

observed.title: Add opt-in features to a shared primitive as isolated render paths
observed.statement: When extending a widely-used primitive (a table with hundreds of call sites), mount each opt-in feature as its own render path — a separate body component, props that are no-ops when unset — and state the contract in a comment: the default branches stay byte-identical for every consumer that doesn't opt in. This is what makes big shared primitives safe to extend.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/UnifiedTable.tsx:519-527,691-699` — "Sticky-group-header mode is an isolated render path (GroupedTableBody) so the default virtual/non-virtual branches below stay byte-identical for the many tables that don't opt in"; same contract stated for `scrollRestoreKey`/`nodeMeta` and in `FacetedDecisionTable.tsx:62-71`.

observed.title: Apply CSS containment to every table row
observed.statement: Stamp `contain: 'layout paint style'` on each row of long lists and tables so layout and paint invalidation from an in-row change never escapes the row — cheap insurance that keeps virtualized and animated lists smooth.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/UnifiedTable.tsx:647,674,803` and `DataGrid.tsx:379` — every row style includes `contain: 'layout paint style'` alongside the grid template.

observed.title: scale-* transforms do not resize the layout box — size illustrations with real dimensions
observed.statement: A transform-scaled element still measures its pre-transform size: a `scale-[3.25]` watermark measured 48px while painting 156px, overflowing onto the heading. Give illustrations a real layout box (`w-24 h-24`) and choose deliberately which element yields under pressure — withhold `shrink-0` from the art and grant it to the heading, so a short pane clips the picture, never the message.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/IllustratedEmptyState.tsx:230-266` — "A real 96x96 layout box, NOT a transform-scaled 48px one: `scale-*` does not resize the layout box … Deliberately NOT `shrink-0`, while the heading above IS: in a short pane something has to give, and it must never be the message." (2026-07-27 rewrite after the overflow shipped.)

observed.title: Mint DOM ids with useId, never Math.random in useMemo
observed.statement: Generating a DOM/SVG-defs id from `Math.random()` inside `useMemo` is non-deterministic (hostile to SSR/hydration and snapshots) and carries a real collision probability across many instances — while React ships `useId()` for exactly this. The repo demonstrates the drift: one component random-generates its gradient id while every neighbouring file already uses useId.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/display/ConfidenceArc.tsx:42-43` — `const gradientId = useMemo(() => \`conf-arc-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}\`, []);` — while `MotionizedGlyph`, `Tooltip`, and `DensityToggle` in the same directory use `useId()`.

observed.title: Split live onChange from settle-only onCommit on continuous inputs
observed.statement: Sliders and steppers should expose two callbacks with an explicit contract: `onChange` fires per tick/keystroke for live preview; `onCommit` fires once when the interaction settles (blur / Enter / pointer release) and ONLY if the value actually changed since interaction start — so expensive side effects (persistence, IPC) run once per gesture. Capture the start value in a ref and mark committed so a trailing blur after drag-release can't double-fire. Derive display precision from the step and round each clamp, or repeated +0.01 steps produce 0.30000000000000004.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/Slider.tsx:7-12,56-71` and `NumberStepper.tsx:13-17,96-105` — "Mark committed so a trailing blur after a drag-release doesn't double-fire"; float-drift guard `stepDecimals('0.01') → 2` drives `toFixed` (`NumberStepper.tsx:38-44,71-80`, "Round to the step's precision to avoid binary float drift"). Both contracts test-asserted in `__tests__/NumberStepper.test.tsx:69-74,106-132` and `__tests__/Slider.test.tsx:44-70`.

observed.title: Guard hold-to-repeat loops against buttons that become disabled mid-hold
observed.statement: A press-and-hold repeat loop must refuse to start if the first step is already a no-op, and must end itself from inside its own tick when a step fails — because a button that becomes `disabled` mid-hold never fires pointerup/pointerleave, so the timer would outlive the gesture and spin forever.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/NumberStepper.tsx:137-160` — "don't schedule a loop that would spin forever once the button becomes `disabled` (a disabled button never fires pointerup/pointerleave, so the loop would otherwise outlive the interaction)."

observed.title: Suppress the parent echo in lossy controlled round-trips with a last-emitted ref
observed.statement: When a controlled editor's serialization is lossy (a keyless-but-valued row is dropped by rows→JSON), the parent echoing your own output back would re-derive local state from the lossy form and wipe in-progress edits. Record the exact string last emitted; when the incoming value equals it, skip re-deriving.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/KeyValueEditor.tsx:51-71` — "`rowsToJson` can't represent a keyless-but-valued row (it drops it), so a round trip through the parent … would otherwise re-derive `rows` from that lossy JSON and wipe local edits made before a key was typed."

observed.title: Split a form-error registry into a stable writer context and a reader context, and jump to fields without a focus fight
observed.statement: A form-error summary needs two contexts: a stable-identity registration context every field consumes (register/unregister — never changes identity, so error churn doesn't re-render every field) and a separate errors-list context only the summary banner reads. Registration is idempotent and unregisters on unmount so conditional fields don't linger. "Jump to field" pairs smooth `scrollIntoView` with `focus({ preventScroll: true })` so the browser's instant focus-scroll doesn't fight the smooth scroll.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/FormErrorContext.tsx:10-21,56-68` — "Its value never changes identity, so adding/removing errors does NOT re-render every field"; `FormErrorSummary.tsx:27-36` — "preventScroll: the smooth scroll above owns positioning; focus() must not fight it with an instant jump"; field registration gated on the visible error only in `FormField.tsx:182-198`; test coverage `__tests__/FormErrorSummary.test.tsx:65-102`.

observed.title: Default validation display to first-blur, and contain blur within the field wrapper
observed.statement: Show a field's error only after the user first leaves it, then live — the researched default (NN/g, GOV.UK, Material) — with `'change'`/`'submit'` policies and a submit-time force override as escape hatches. Crucially, the wrapper's onBlur must ignore focus moves BETWEEN inner elements (input → its adornment button) via `currentTarget.contains(relatedTarget)`, or clicking the reveal icon marks the field touched.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/FormField.tsx:34-46,155-161,231-237` — `validateOn` policy citing the three design systems; "Mark interacted only when focus leaves the FormField entirely, not when moving between inner elements (e.g. an input + adornment button)."

observed.title: Replay a CSS keyframe with the remove-class → force-reflow → re-add idiom, once per codebase
observed.statement: The only reliable way to re-trigger a CSS animation is: remove the class, force a reflow (`void el.offsetWidth`), re-add the class, and clean up on `animationend { once: true }`. Codify it as one exported helper/hook — this repo factored the same idiom four ways (a hook, an exported helper, and two inline copies), which is the argument for sanctioning a single implementation.
observed.detail_md: Evidence ×4: `src/features/shared/components/forms/useShakeError.ts:11-25` ("Force reflow so the browser treats the re-add as a new animation"), `SortableColumnHeader.tsx:19-25` (`columnSortPulse`), `CharBudget.tsx:32-45`, `FormField.tsx:201-214`.

observed.title: Extract portal anchoring into one hook, with capture-phase scroll tracking and an explicit z contract against the modal stack
observed.statement: Every portalled dropdown/select re-implements the same getBoundingClientRect + scroll/resize dance; extract it once with (a) the scroll listener in CAPTURE phase so scrollable ancestors are caught, (b) opt-in flip-up and a bottomMargin separate from gap to preserve call-site clearance, and (c) a documented z-index that must clear the modal stack's computed range — or options render UNDER the modal that owns them.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/useAnchoredPortalPosition.ts:12-64` — "Extracted from ThemedSelect's FilterableSelect and Listbox's portal mode, which each re-implemented this … dance independently (refactor-bughunt-2026-07-10 #7)"; `ThemedSelect.tsx:165-167` — "z must clear portal-mode BaseModals (Z_INDEX_PORTAL_BASE = 10000 + depth*10) so the options never render UNDER the modal they're in."

observed.title: No backdrop-blur on sticky headers — the compositor re-samples it into a flicker
observed.statement: `backdrop-filter` re-samples its backdrop on every compositor frame, and hover/pointer repaints generate those frames — so in WebView2 a frosted sticky header flickers as a blinking white band across every module header. Use a solid/semi-transparent background on sticky chrome instead; the lesson had to be learned twice (page background, then header) so it's recorded at both sites.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/layout/ContentLayout.tsx:161-169` — "No `backdrop-blur` here. backdrop-filter re-samples its backdrop on every compositor frame … so in WebView2 the frosted layer flickers as a blinking white band across every module header"; the skeleton twin `ContentHeaderSkeleton.tsx:47-48` carries a pointer back to this note.

observed.title: Build skeletons as explicit twins: copied chrome classes, em-sized bars inside real typo line boxes
observed.statement: A loading skeleton earns zero layout shift by being a maintained TWIN of the real component: deliberately COPY the real class list (with an in-file instruction to update the twin in the same change — sharing would couple styling refactors), size placeholder bars in `em` INSIDE the real `typo-*` line boxes so height is truthful, and default to a calm variant (static, low-contrast, no pulse). Table skeletons take a column spec mirroring the real grid, plus a stacked mobile variant.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/layout/ContentHeaderSkeleton.tsx:3-30,59-68` — "The class lists below are intentionally copied from ContentHeader rather than shared — **if you restyle ContentHeader, update this twin in the same change.**"; `TableSkeleton.tsx:18-25,79-92` — `columns: { span, width, alignRight }[]` mirroring the 12-col grid, `<md` stacked variant; calm default across `ListSkeleton.tsx`/`TableSkeleton.tsx`.

observed.title: Defer heavy subtrees behind a priority ladder with a synchronous test escape hatch
observed.statement: Wrap expensive non-critical subtrees in a defer component with a small priority ladder — `idle` (requestIdleCallback + timeout), `next-frame` (rAF), `mount-after` (setTimeout) — with a setTimeout(0) fallback where rIC is absent, and an `immediate` prop that renders synchronously so RTL/snapshot tests stay deterministic. Motivated by the webview hanging on large single React commits.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/layout/DeferUntilIdle.tsx:3-33,62-89` — three priorities, 500ms rIC timeout, "Test-only escape hatch. When `true`, children render synchronously on mount regardless of priority." Fully covered including a spied rIC in `DeferUntilIdle.test.tsx:41-90`.

observed.title: Suffix every framer layoutId with a per-instance useId
observed.statement: Two mounted instances of a component sharing a literal `layoutId` make the shared-layout indicator teleport/animate BETWEEN the instances. Namespace every layoutId with a per-instance `useId()` suffix — this repo enforces it independently in four components, which is the tell that it belongs in review checklists.
observed.detail_md: Evidence ×4: `src/features/shared/components/layout/PanelTabBar.tsx:40-43` — "Per-instance suffix so two tab bars never share a framer-motion layoutId — a shared id makes the underline teleport/animate between the two bars"; same in `SegmentedTabs.tsx:39-41`, `forms/PillGroup.tsx:40-41`, `layout/settings/SettingsScaffold.tsx:56,78-79`.

observed.title: Tablists get roving tabindex with arrow/Home/End over enabled tabs, and export the panel-side props
observed.statement: A tab bar is one Tab stop: `tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1}` per tab, Arrow/Home/End moving focus AND selection with modular wraparound over only the enabled tabs. Export a `tabPanelProps()` helper so the `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby` pairing on the panel side can't drift from the tabs' generated ids.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/layout/PanelTabBar.tsx:46-70,82-84` ("without it every tab sat in the Tab order and arrow keys did nothing") and `SegmentedTabs.tsx:44-99,176-182` — `segmentedTabPanelProps()` exported for the panel half of the ARIA pairing.

observed.title: Never nest interactive elements — render secondary actions as siblings or role-button spans
observed.statement: Nesting a real control inside a `<button>` is invalid HTML, breaks hydration, and the inner control swallows the outer's click. Render a card/row action as a SIBLING of the toggle button; when a clickable must live visually inside a button (orbit dots on a sidebar button), use a `span role="button" tabIndex={0}` with Enter/Space handling and stopPropagation instead of a nested `<button>`.
observed.detail_md: Evidence ×3: `src/features/shared/components/layout/SectionCard.tsx:185-191` — "nesting interactive elements is invalid HTML (the inner one also swallows the toggle's click)"; `forms/SettingRow.tsx:61-63,88` — whole-row hit target with exactly one focusable control and stopPropagation on the toggle; `chrome/sidebar/OrbitDots.tsx:86-108` — "Rendered as span+role='button' rather than <button>. SidebarLevel1 wraps each section in a <button>, and nesting a real button inside is an HTML hydration error. Keyboard & a11y are preserved via role, tabIndex, and onKeyDown."

observed.title: Unlayered token classes beat Tailwind utilities — change the token, not the call site
observed.statement: When a design system ships its typography as unlayered CSS classes (`typo-*`), local Tailwind utility overrides silently lose the cascade: a `font-normal`/opacity patch applied at a call site has no effect at all. The durable fix for a styling change is editing the token definition, and the failed-patch history is worth recording at the site that tempted it.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/SettingRow.tsx:76-82` — "No local overrides — utilities can't beat the unlayered typo tokens anyway (that's how an earlier font-normal/85 patch silently failed here)."

observed.title: Scroll-spy binds the real scroll parent up-front and never gates on current overflow
observed.statement: A section scroll-spy must walk ancestors for `overflow-y: auto|scroll|overlay` (window fallback) at bind time and deliberately NOT check `scrollHeight > clientHeight` — content often grows after mount (async panels), so gating on current overflow permanently disables the spy. Memoize per-id callback-ref setters so tagging a section never churns the ref, and compute container-relative jump deltas rather than scrollIntoView when a scroll parent exists.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/layout/settings/useSectionScrollSpy.ts:3-19,39-45,77-88` — "We deliberately do NOT gate on a current `scrollHeight > clientHeight`: settings sections often grow after mount (async-loaded panels)".

observed.title: Auto-re-mask revealed secrets on a focus-aware timer and keep the reveal toggle out of the Tab order
observed.statement: A password/key field that the user reveals should re-mask itself on a timer (~8s) that only runs while focus is OUTSIDE the field — never re-mask a key mid-read — capping shoulder-surf exposure without fighting intent. Reserve input padding so text can't slide under the icon, and put the toggle at `tabIndex={-1}` with `aria-pressed` so keyboard flow goes field-to-field.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/PasswordToggleField.tsx:6-19,61-94,104-114` — timer cleared while focused ("an actively-read key is never re-masked mid-glance"), `pr-10` reservation, `tabIndex={-1}` + `aria-pressed`; "This caps shoulder-surf exposure without fighting the user's intent."

observed.title: Auto-grow textareas in useLayoutEffect, resetting height to auto first
observed.statement: Auto-growing a textarea needs both halves: reset height to `auto` before reading scrollHeight (scrollHeight never reports smaller than the current height, so the field could otherwise never shrink), and measure in `useLayoutEffect` — a passive effect makes the field visibly lag a fast typist by one character.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/ChatInputBar.tsx:85-97,118-121` — both rationales documented inline: "measuring in a passive effect makes the field visibly lag a fast typist by one character."

observed.title: Don't hardcode the literal a named constant already exports
observed.statement: Exporting `DEFAULT_PERSONA_COLOR` and then hardcoding `'#8b5cf6'` three more times in the same file (fallback, reset target, reset-button visibility check) means changing the default silently breaks reset behaviour. The moment a value earns a name, every other occurrence must reference it — grep for the literal before merging.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/forms/ColorPicker.tsx:22,108,127,130` — `export const DEFAULT_PERSONA_COLOR` at the top; `{value && value !== '#8b5cf6' && (…)}` below. Adjacent damage in the same pocket: `TableSelector.tsx:167` pluralizes the footer on `tables.length` (the total) while the sentence is about `selectedTables.length`.

observed.title: Lazy-load libraries that inspect child identity via one render-prop wrapper, not per-component React.lazy
observed.statement: Libraries like recharts match children by component identity (`child.type === Bar`), so wrapping each export in its own `React.lazy` silently breaks composition — the Suspense wrapper fails the identity check. Use one dynamic import for the whole library exposed through a render-prop wrapper: a single shared chunk, and normal child composition inside the callback.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/charts/RechartsWrapper.tsx:3-20` — "Render-prop API instead of per-component React.lazy wrappers because recharts inspects child component identity (e.g. `child.type === Bar`) — a Suspense-wrapped child fails that check."

observed.title: Queue and space aria-live announcements; never setState them directly
observed.statement: A burst of screen-reader announcements in one tick collapses under React batching — only the LAST message reaches the live region and intermediates are never spoken. Queue announcements, drain on an interval (~150ms) so the reader finishes each utterance, and bump a key per message so identical consecutive messages force a DOM change and are re-spoken. When exposing an imperative module-level announce handle, clear it on unmount only if it is still YOURS — blind nulling after a remount silences announcements for the session.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/feedback/AriaLiveProvider.tsx:35-59,74-79` — "React coalesces the setState calls so only the LAST message reaches the live region — intermediate messages are dropped and never spoken"; guarded cleanup `if (_announce === announce) _announce = null;`.

observed.title: Parse LLM-emitted UI specs forgiving-in bounded-out, with a per-item salvage pass that reports drops
observed.statement: Schema-validate agent-emitted structures with coercing, clamping, truncating field types (percent clamps rather than rejects; text coerces primitives and truncates); strict-parse the whole document first, and on failure salvage every individually valid block, surface the dropped count to the user rather than hiding it, and fail only when NOTHING renderable survives — at which point fall back to plain markdown.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/surface/surfaceSpec.ts:26-55,224-266` — "a hallucinated block type never takes down an otherwise sound surface. Fails only when nothing renderable survives, at which point callers fall back to MarkdownRenderer"; the dropped count renders via `data-testid="surface-dropped-note"` (`SurfaceRenderer.tsx:122-126`); tests `__tests__/surfaceSpec.test.ts:102-115`.

observed.title: Let agents emit UI only through a frozen vocabulary mapped 1:1 onto blessed components — and test that nothing auto-runs
observed.statement: Agent-generated UI is injection-free and on-brand by construction when every emitted block type renders through exactly one existing catalog component — no arbitrary HTML, the switch IS the entire vocabulary, extension = new block + schema + one case. Pair it with an executable invariant that agent-proposed actions only ever set pending state: tests assert the consent surface opens ONLY after an explicit click and the execute mock was never called.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/surface/SurfaceRenderer.tsx:1-13,176-279` — "The switch below is the ENTIRE vocabulary — every node maps onto an existing catalog component, no new visual primitives, no arbitrary HTML"; contract doc `surface/SPEC.md:1-7,29-43`; invariant test `__tests__/SurfaceRenderer.test.tsx:103-127` — `it('never auto-runs: dispatch opens the chooser only after an explicit click')` with `expect(executePersonaMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.

observed.title: Centralize agent-dispatch consent into one surface with a pre-flight prepare() that aborts on failure
observed.statement: When several transports can hand work to an agent, route them all through one consent surface (editable prompt, radiogroup semantics, dedup against already-running sessions) that accepts a `prepare()` hook running AFTER user confirm but BEFORE the transport — throwing aborts the dispatch, so a half-prepared target never gets a session pointed at it. Document deliberate asymmetries (no dedup for transports the app holds no handle on).

observed.title: Namespace drag payloads by custom MIME and clear drag state on drop, not only dragend
observed.statement: Kanban-style drag needs three guards: a custom MIME type so foreign drags are inert and `dragOver` can reject before preventDefault; `dragLeave` ignoring bubbles from descendants via relatedTarget containment; and clearing the dragging id in `onDrop` — when the drop moves the card to another column, the source element unmounts before its native `dragend` ever fires, leaving the moved card stuck at drag opacity.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/kanban/KanbanBoard.tsx:96-123` — "Clear the drag state here, not just in onDragEnd: when the drop moves the card to another column, the original element unmounts before its native `dragend` fires … the moved card would stay stuck at opacity-40."

observed.title: Keep a rAF loop alive across prop changes by calling the tick through a ref
observed.statement: If a driver effect schedules `requestAnimationFrame(tick)` directly, it must depend on `tick` — whose identity changes whenever its inputs change — cancelling and failing to reschedule the loop mid-run. Store the latest tick in a ref the loop calls through, so the driver effect's deps stay stable and the animation survives estimate/prop updates. Pair with an honest progress model: linear to ~85% over the estimate, asymptotic crawl to ~98%, an over-estimate warning state, and 100% only on real completion.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/progress/EstimatedProgressBar.tsx:61-84` — "Keep the latest tick in a ref so the driver effect below doesn't need to depend on it (tick's identity changes whenever estimatedSeconds changes, which would otherwise cancel and fail to reschedule the rAF loop mid-run)"; honesty model at `:43-57,89-93`.

observed.title: Virtualize streaming logs with threshold-based sticky-bottom and typed pre-output states
observed.statement: A live log panel should virtualize variable-height lines (measureElement), decide auto-scroll stickiness by a small bottom-distance threshold (~10px), show a jump-to-bottom affordance with an unseen-line counter only when the user has scrolled away, and replace the single generic empty state with a typed one — idle / connecting / queued-with-position / failed — because "no output yet" means different things.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/terminal/TerminalBody.tsx:9-15,39-101,116-150,259-273` — useVirtualizer with measureElement, 10px stick threshold, unseen-count FAB, typed `idle | connecting | {queued, position} | failed` empty states.

observed.title: Keep shared primitives store-free by taking capability slots from the host
observed.statement: A shared component library stays domain-free when primitives receive capabilities as slots instead of importing app stores: an ErrorBoundary takes `onGoHome`, a renderer takes `onExecutePersona` and renders actions disabled-with-explanation when absent, a destructive-confirm takes `blastRadius` as a ReactNode the host fetched, a board takes `renderCard`. The host owns fetching and wiring; the primitive owns behaviour — which is exactly what lets it live in a catalog.
observed.detail_md: Evidence ×4: `src/features/shared/components/feedback/ErrorBoundary.tsx:18-20,98-111` (injected `onGoHome`, hard-navigation last resort); `surface/SurfaceRenderer.tsx:32-47,63-76` (context slots, disabled-with-tooltip when absent); `overlays/ConfirmDestructiveModal.tsx:19-22` ("host owns fetching + rendering so this modal stays a domain-free primitive"); `kanban/KanbanBoard.tsx:36-57` (`renderCard`/`renderEmptyColumn`).

observed.title: Normalize repeated human decisions onto one record type and one action control, with tone rationale recorded
observed.statement: When several features grow accept/reject queues, unify them on one domain-free DecisionRecord/DecisionTone vocabulary and one actions component whose closed tone map makes a fourth tone impossible to invent. Record the interaction rationale, not just styling — e.g. reject stays visually quiet until hover because "a destructive-looking reject button makes reviewers hesitate on a queue they are supposed to burn down", and "the row opens; the buttons decide".
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/decisions/decisionTypes.ts:1-13` (three streams had three layouts and three colour languages), `DecisionActions.tsx:1-21` (TONE_PROPS closed map + hover rationale), `DecisionRow.tsx:76-82` (row-click vs verdict-click contract).

observed.title: A 'single source of truth' comment without landed consumers is a lie the next reader trusts
observed.statement: Declaring a shared primitive the SSOT ("the two named components are thin wrappers") while both consumers still exist as full independent implementations leaves three near-identical config maps drifting, conflicting exported types with the same name, and one copy hardcoding English while the others translate. A consolidation PR must delete or actually re-implement the wrappers — or not write the comment.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/feedback/Banner.tsx:6-16` claims `ErrorRecoveryBanner`/`InlineErrorBanner` are thin wrappers; in reality `InlineErrorBanner.tsx:21-46` (`TIER`) and `ErrorRecoveryBanner.tsx:27-58` (`SEVERITY_CONFIG`) are full duplicates; `ErrorRecoveryBanner` hardcodes `aria-label="Dismiss"`/`label: 'Retry'` (`:55-57,100-108`) while the others use `t.common.*`; two conflicting `BannerSeverity` types are exported (`Banner.tsx:16` vs `InlineErrorBanner.tsx:6`).

observed.title: Two components with the same name and divergent classifiers — an import typo silently changes behavior
observed.statement: The repo carries two `TerminalBody.tsx` files with the same export name: one uses the shared terminal line classifier/style map, the other defines a local substring-matching classifier with a different colour language. An import-path typo silently swaps classification rules, and terminal styling is maintained twice. Shared classification belongs in one module; if two components must share a name, one should re-export or delegate to the other.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/progress/TerminalBody.tsx:8-23` (local `LINE_STYLES` + `classifyLine` substring-matching `'error'`, `'[system]'`, `'complete'`) vs `src/features/shared/components/terminal/TerminalBody.tsx:4-7` (shared `TERMINAL_STYLE_MAP` / `useTerminalClassification` from `@/lib/utils/terminalColors`).

observed.title: Version consent records, compare for equality, and badge only the newly disclosed sections on re-prompt
observed.statement: A first-use consent stored as key-presence can never be re-asked. Store `{version}` and compare for EQUALITY (not presence) so bumping the constant re-prompts; export the literal so admin surfaces don't re-declare it; on a version bump, open and badge only the sections that are new since the accepted version, and order plain-language reassurance before admin-grade detail (a defect traced to jargon-first ordering).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/shared/components/overlays/FirstUseConsentModal.tsx:25-58,182-184,244-262` — `CONSENT_KEY` + `CONSENT_VERSION` equality check, every localStorage access try/caught, `isVersionBump` opens + badges new sections, ordering fix tagged `(UAT P10 F-CONSENT-JARGON)`.

observed.title: Hold hand-typed secrets in a ref with a version counter, never in React state
observed.statement: Secret field values (API keys, passwords, client secrets) must live in a useRef with a bumped version counter as the re-render trigger, because useState contents get serialized into React DevTools, Sentry payloads and error-boundary dumps. Pin the behavior with a regression test asserting typing and submit still work.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/forms/CredentialEditForm.tsx:55-69` — "Hand-typed API keys/passwords live in a ref, never React state — mirrors the OAuth hooks ... specifically to avoid exposing them via React DevTools / Sentry error serialization". Same in `src/features/vault/shared/hooks/useCredentialOAuth.ts:25-26` and `useGoogleOAuth.ts:24-26` (`getValues`/`valuesVersion`). Regression test: `forms/__tests__/CredentialEditForm.test.tsx`.

observed.title: Reference position, never content, in errors from secret-bearing parsers
observed.statement: Parse errors over input that may contain secrets must cite only line/index, never a snippet. Echoing even 40 chars of an unparsable .env line leaked secret-shaped content into user-visible toasts and Sentry payloads.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/import/importHelpers.ts:174-188` — "The previous error included the first 40 chars of the offending line, which leaked secret-shaped content ... into the user-visible toast and the React error boundary's Sentry payload"; now `errors.push(`Line ${i + 1}: missing '=' separator`)`. Preview renders values masked to a 4-char prefix (`ImportPreview.tsx:128-130`).

observed.title: Mask discovered secrets at the point of read; re-read raw values only at commit
observed.statement: A credential scanner should mask each value in the same scope it reads it and drop the plaintext immediately — raw secrets never accumulate in intermediate collections, cross IPC, or reach the render layer. Only the import/commit path re-reads the real value, after validating the item id as a safe path component.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/foraging.rs:179-219` — "Values are masked immediately on read — raw secrets are never accumulated in intermediate collections, preventing plaintext exposure in memory dumps"; import re-reads at `:710-733` with "The fields HashMap contains raw secret material — never log or emit it" and `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all)]`; hostile-id guards `is_safe_path_component` (`:779-781`) and `ALLOWED_DOTENV_SOURCES` (`:784`). UI renders only masked fields (`ForagingResultCard.tsx:130-138`).

observed.title: Encode the exact winning source into a discovered item's id; never re-derive at import
observed.statement: When discovery resolves one of several ambiguous sources (GH_TOKEN vs GITHUB_TOKEN), embed the winner in the item id. Re-deriving from a category at commit time re-runs the last-writer-wins scan and can import a different value than the one the user reviewed and approved.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/foraging.rs:188-194` — "...instead of re-deriving from service_type at import time (which would re-scan ALL matching vars and silently last-writer-wins again — possibly picking a different value than what was shown/masked here if the environment changed between scan and import)"; id built as `env:{service_type}:{chosen_keys}` (`:241`), consumed at `:808-855` with a documented legacy fallback.

observed.title: A scanner must distinguish 'source absent' from 'source unreadable'
observed.statement: Silently skipping an unreadable file makes a permissions problem look like a missing integration. Return None for NotFound, push a source token onto an error list for any other I/O error, and surface the deduped list so the UI can say 'couldn't read X' instead of omitting a source the user expected.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/foraging.rs:148-166` `fn read_if_present` — `Err(e) if e.kind() == NotFound => None, Err(_) => { errors.push(source_token) ... }`; contract documented on the result type at `:67-72`: "Absent files are NOT reported — only real read failures". Used by 6 scanners plus a read_dir variant (`:561-568`).

observed.title: Sanitize secret-echoing provider error bodies inside the error constructor, pinned by leak tests
observed.statement: Token/auth endpoints echo submitted secrets (client_secret, refresh_token) or issue fresh token material inside error envelopes. Run the body through the redactor at the single place the error value is built — so message, body, logs, audit and IPC are all covered — and pin it with a test asserting the secret is absent while diagnostic context survives.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:86-106` — "A failed token-endpoint response can echo back the submitted `client_secret` / `refresh_token`, or issue fresh token material inside an error envelope ... so the body must be sanitized at this single chokepoint before any of them see it". Test at `:2312-2338` asserts neither `message` nor `body` carries the secret while `invalid_grant` context survives. Same `sanitize_secrets` reused in `src-tauri/src/engine/healthcheck.rs:1143,1157`.

observed.title: Strip the request URL out of HTTP client errors before logging or displaying them
observed.statement: Dynamic base URLs can embed a secret in the path or query (.../bot{token}, ?apikey=...), and reqwest::Error's Display includes the URL. Call .without_url() on every error-to-string conversion so failure detail survives without the secret-bearing URL.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/api_proxy.rs:885-889` — "dynamic base URLs can embed a secret in the path... `.without_url()` preserves the failure detail without the secret-bearing URL"; same on the retry path `:918-922` and in `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/credential_design.rs:279-284`.

observed.title: Truncate display strings on char boundaries, never byte offsets
observed.statement: Byte-slicing a string to cap a debug/preview payload panics on multi-byte content (emoji, CJK, accents). Find the truncation point with char_indices so hostile or merely international input cannot crash the backend.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/query_debug.rs:121-136` — "Uses char_indices to find a safe UTF-8 boundary instead of slicing at byte offsets, which would panic on multi-byte characters (emoji, CJK, accented)". Sits inside the debug-payload capping pipeline (`DEBUG_MAX_RESULT_ROWS`, `rows_omitted`).

observed.title: A runaway-loop cap must kill the process at the crossing, not log a warning
observed.statement: A max-iterations guard that only queues a warning does nothing — the stream keeps being consumed until the model stops or the session timeout fires, burning most of the budget. Fire the guard exactly once with == at the boundary and actively tear the child process down.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/auto_cred_browser.rs:1037-1060` — "This check previously only queued a warning — the read loop kept consuming the stream until the model stopped on its own or the 600s session timeout fired ... `==` (not `>=`) fires this exactly once per session, at the crossing." then `if let Some(pid) = registry.take_pid("auto_cred") { kill_pid(pid); }`; `kill_pid` shared with the cancel command (`:1579-1613`).

observed.title: Treat LLM stream-json assistant events as cumulative and emit only the computed delta
observed.statement: Claude CLI stream-json assistant events re-send the whole turn's text every time; forwarding them naively duplicates every line downstream. Keep a per-turn accumulator, emit new[acc.len()..] when the new text is a superset, skip subsets, and reset the accumulator when a tool result signals a new turn.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/auto_cred_browser.rs:204-261` — "Claude CLI `stream-json` sends cumulative `assistant` events — each contains ALL text from the current turn, not just the delta"; reset hook at `:1088-1095` on `StreamLineType::ToolResult`. Six unit tests at `:1755-1823` pin superset/subset/reset behavior.

observed.title: Nest deadlines so the process owner always wins the timeout race
observed.statement: When a frontend IPC timeout wraps a backend that spawns a long-running child, keep the backend's hard timeout strictly below the frontend's so the failure is a clean typed error and a killed child — a frontend timeout that fires first abandons a live process. Both sides document the ordering.
observed.detail_md: Evidence, backend side: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/auto_cred_browser.rs:35-46` — "Kept just under the frontend IPC timeout ... so the backend always wins the race and returns a clean error rather than the frontend abandoning a live process" (`BROWSER_TIMEOUT_SECS: 600`). Frontend side: `src/api/vault/autoCredBrowser.ts:8-18` — "Kept 1 min ABOVE the backend's 10-minute hard process timeout ... must not fire before the backend has had its chance to kill the process (which would orphan a live CLI)" (`BROWSER_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS = 11 * 60 * 1000`).

observed.title: Sweep temp files and orphan grandchildren explicitly — RAII cleanup never runs when you are killed
observed.statement: NamedTempFile Drop and child reaping do not happen on SIGKILL/Task-Manager kills, and spawned driver servers leave their own children (Chromium, 200-500 MB each) behind. Sweep prefixed temp files at session start and pattern-kill orphan grandchildren at session end.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/auto_cred_browser.rs:1435-1453` — "`NamedTempFile` auto-deletes on Drop, but that won't run if the process is killed ... We sweep the OS temp dir at session start"; `:1455-1488` `cleanup_orphaned_browsers()` — "Chromium child may remain running and consume 200-500 MB of memory per instance", using `Get-CimInstance` because "WMIC is deprecated and absent on many ARM64 installs".

observed.title: Spawn detection probes with a cleared, allowlisted environment and byte-capped output readers
observed.statement: External tool probes should run with env_clear() plus a minimal allowlisted environment (no ambient secrets reach the child), read stdout/stderr through a take()-bounded reader so a malicious binary cannot exhaust memory, and hide the console window on Windows.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/auth_detect.rs:27-29` `MAX_CLI_OUTPUT_BYTES: 256 * 1024` ("Prevents memory exhaustion if a malicious binary produces unbounded output"); `:242-249` `read_limited` via `reader.take(limit as u64)`; `:498-536` `sanitized_env()`. Reused with the same shape in `cli_capture.rs:624-689` (STEP_TIMEOUT = 5s, kill on both pipe-failure and timeout arms).

observed.title: Keep credential-capture command specs as compile-time constants, and never let a static sensitivity flag be the only log guard
observed.statement: Subprocess invocations that touch credentials are built from &'static spec tables whose args never interpolate user input or catalog data. And even where the table marks fields sensitive, do not log the 'non-sensitive' branch's value — a future row added without the flag would leak silently. Spec completeness is enforced by tests.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/cli_capture.rs:7-14` — "capture specs are compile-time constants, never loaded from the catalog or user input"; `:44-47` "Arguments passed verbatim. Must never interpolate user input."; `:729-742` — "No `value = %value` here: the only guard against a secret leak on this branch is `cf.sensitive` on the static `CAPTURE_SPECS` table, and that guard can regress ... keep the log audit-only". Invariant tests at `:1070-1124`, `:1168-1179`.

observed.title: Map a new failure mode onto the recovery pipeline that already exists
observed.statement: When a new failure is semantically identical to an old one (a dead CLI session is the CLI equivalent of a revoked OAuth grant), convert it into that existing error variant so all downstream healing — ledger flag, event, OS notification, vault banner, auto-resolve — fires for free, instead of inventing a parallel path that silently backs off.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/cli_capture.rs:588-598` — "Classifying it as OAuthRevoked lets the refresh engine's existing needs-reauth pipeline (ledger flag + event + OS notification + vault banner) fire instead of silently backing off while personas keep executing with a dead token." Locked by test `unauthenticated_maps_to_oauth_revoked` (`:1149-1164`); symmetric success path at `:873-890` resets fail counters and resolves the healing episode.

observed.title: Gate, fingerprint and bound model-authored SQL before executing it
observed.statement: Never execute LLM-generated SQL blindly: classify mutation vs read and refuse mutations unless the user explicitly opted in; audit a fingerprint (length + attempt), never the query text; cap the fix-and-retry loop; and feed each retry the sanitized error plus the user's original question — not the model's last attempt — so intent doesn't drift.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/query_debug.rs:390-412` — `query_fingerprint = format!("len={}, attempt={}")` and "Mutation blocked: enable allow_mutations to permit write queries"; `:173-174` `MAX_RETRIES: 3`; `:509-516` — "Use the original query_text, not the AI-generated query_to_run, so the AI sees the user's original intent on each retry"; retry prompt receives `safe_msg` (`:486-489`). Classifier exposed standalone at `db_schema.rs:164-167`.

observed.title: Apply selecting filters before the top-k cut; only thresholds may come after
observed.statement: Truncating a ranked candidate pool to top_k before a selecting filter (scope/path) returns 'whichever of the global top-k happen to match' — often zero. Carry the bounded pool through filtering and cut afterwards; pure thresholds like min_score remain correct post-cut. Pin both directions with regression tests.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/vector_kb.rs:1063-1073` — "`min_score` is a threshold (post-filtering it is correct), whereas `filter_source` SELECTS a subset: trimming first would hand the caller 'however many of the global top_k happen to live under that path'"; cut moved into `select_search_results` (`:1149-1171`); tests `pre_truncating_the_pool_starves_a_scoped_search` and `filtering_before_the_cut_fills_top_k_in_ranking_order` (`:1636-1663`).

observed.title: Re-validate a stored vector index's embedding model at read time, not only at write time
observed.statement: Recording the model/dimensions an index was built with is useless if queries don't check them. Compare against the live embedder on every search and fail loudly with a remediation instruction ('Re-index to search it') — a silent mismatch yields plausible-but-wrong neighbours, which is worse than an error.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/vector_kb.rs:942-964` — "embedding_model/embedding_dims are recorded at create time but were never re-read on search, so a default-model change ... silently embedded queries with the wrong model — either a hard sqlite-vec dimension error or, worse, plausible-but-wrong neighbours (bug-hunt 2026-06-07 mcp #2)"; belt-and-braces vector-length re-check at `:968-973`; dedicated `kb_reindex` remediation command (`:706-715`).

observed.title: Refuse an operation that would desync two stores; pair the refusal with compensation and a reconciler
observed.statement: When a delete spans a relational table and a secondary (vector) index and the index is unavailable, error out inside the transaction so it rolls back — a partial delete leaves orphans that silently shrink every future result. Complement with create-side compensation ordering (build the easiest-to-roll-back store first) and a startup reconciler whose failed-check default is 'assume it exists, don't delete'.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/vector_kb.rs:1339-1362` — "deleting the chunk and document rows below while leaving their vectors behind would permanently desync ... Refuse the partial delete instead — the transaction rolls back on this early return"; create-side compensation at `:66-120` ("Create vector index first — easiest to roll back"); `reconcile_orphaned_kb_records` (`:1401-1516`) with `unwrap_or(true) // If we can't check, assume it exists (don't delete)`.

observed.title: Degrade optional enrichment to the base result; never let it fail the request
observed.statement: Re-rankers, schema introspection and other enrichment steps get wrapped so every failure mode (serialization, pool checkout, SQL error, empty result) logs a warning and falls through to the primary result — a broken optimizer must not break the feature it optimizes.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/vector_kb.rs:1004-1061` — "Failures here degrade to vector-only ordering — never block the search", with three independent fallbacks (serialize / BM25 query / connection checkout) each yielding an empty rank map so RRF re-rank is skipped. Same posture in `query_debug.rs:210-214` ("best-effort — don't fail if introspection errors") and `nl_query.rs:353-357`.

observed.title: Cap the decompressed size of every archive entry twice — declared size is attacker-controlled
observed.statement: Untrusted archives must be read through both a declared-size check and a take()-bounded reader with a post-read length re-check, because the declared entry size is part of the attacker-controlled input (zip-bomb defence).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/engine/src/enclave.rs:269-320` — `MAX_DECOMPRESSED_SIZE: 50MB`, `if file.size() > MAX_DECOMPRESSED_SIZE {...}` followed by `Read::take(&mut file, MAX_DECOMPRESSED_SIZE + 1)` and a post-read length re-check; the helper serves all three entry reads.

observed.title: Stamp the cadence timestamp before doing the periodic work, and abort if the stamp fails
observed.statement: For run-at-most-once-per-interval jobs, write the last-run marker before starting the sweep: if the run panics or the process dies midway, the next tick still backs off instead of retry-storming. If the timestamp write itself fails, skip the sweep entirely; a missing/corrupt timestamp is treated as due and healed by the write.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/healthcheck.rs:732-770` — "The timestamp is refreshed BEFORE the sweep (retry-storm hardening ...): if the sweep panics or the app dies mid-run, the next tick still backs off"; failed write aborts with "skipping sweep to avoid retry storm". Comment names the same pattern in `digest_tick`.

observed.title: Recover a poisoned lock by clearing the cached entry and surfacing the anomaly — never unwrap()
observed.statement: A poisoned Mutex/RwLock around a cache must be recovered (into_inner/clear_poison), the possibly-torn entry dropped so later reads repopulate from the source of truth, and the regression reported (log + returned error) — unwrap() would turn one panic into a crash for every later caller, silent recovery would serve stale data forever.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/api_proxy.rs:49-67`, `:133-160` — "Clearing cached entry and recovering the lock so subsequent reads repopulate from the database" plus a returned `AppError::Internal` "so the caller (and Sentry) sees the regression rather than silently consuming stale data". Softer variant in `oauth_refresh.rs:1016-1018`: "a panic in another refresh task must not take down the entire background refresh loop via `unwrap()`".

observed.title: On a 401 from an OAuth-backed call, force one refresh-and-retry — and drop your lock first
observed.statement: A locally 'valid' access token can still be rejected (server-side revocation, clock skew), and the normal resolve path trusts local expiry so it will never refresh. Do exactly one forced token exchange + retry; release the per-credential refresh lock before calling the refresh helper (it re-acquires the same lock), and make force=true also evict the cached token or the retry re-uses the stale one.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/api_proxy.rs:891-936` — "the normal resolve path won't refresh (it trusts the local expiry) ... We drop our oauth_refresh_lock first because refresh_single_credential acquires the same per-credential lock (re-entrant acquire would deadlock)".
