observed.title: When the provider has already burned the old token, retry the local commit until it sticks
observed.statement: The moment a provider returns a rotated refresh token, the old one is dead — a transient local persistence failure (keyring lock, seal hiccup, full WAL) must not drop the new token or the credential is permanently bricked with no auto-recovery. Retry the commit with backoff and verify the write with a round-trip read inside the same transaction.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/oauth_refresh.rs:609-686` — "the provider has ALREADY invalidated the old refresh_token the moment it returned the new one ... would otherwise leave the DB holding the dead old token and brick the credential permanently"; `MAX_PERSIST_ATTEMPTS = 3`, `sleep(150ms * attempt)`, `verify_field_roundtrip_on_conn` in-tx. Deliberately duplicated for the resolve path at `:306-392`.

observed.title: Clamp caller-supplied lifetimes into a server-owned window with max, default and floor
observed.statement: Short-livedness is a security property, not a suggestion: the mint path clamps requested TTLs to a hard cap, applies a sane default when unspecified, and enforces a non-zero floor so a mistyped 0 doesn't mint an instantly-dead handle. Absolute expiry is stamped server-side, never trusted from the client clock.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/credential_broker.rs:40-46` — "Hard cap on a derived handle's lifetime — 24 hours. 'Short-lived' is a security property, not a suggestion; the mint path clamps, never trusts." plus `MIN_HANDLE_TTL_MINUTES = 5`; `clamp_handle_ttl` (`:118-123`) with test (`:275-280`). Parallel in `commands/credentials/external_api_keys.rs:28-32` — "we stamp the absolute timestamp here rather than trust the client clock".

observed.title: Validate the system clock before minting anything time-bound
observed.statement: If SystemTime::now() predates the epoch, timestamp helpers silently fabricate 0 and every freshness check downstream fails with a misleading symptom (e.g. 'Authorization took too long'). Check clock sanity once at mint time and fail with the real cause.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:440-456` — "the minted OAuth state instantly fails its own freshness check on callback, and every flow is rejected with a misleading 'Authorization took too long' that sends the user chasing the wrong cause"; `ensure_valid_clock()?` at both mint sites (`:606`, `:1770`).

observed.title: Pin auto-discovered OAuth endpoints to the issuer's own host
observed.statement: A tampered OIDC discovery document can redirect authorization codes and client secrets to an attacker's server. Validate the issuer itself against localhost/private/CGNAT ranges, then require every discovered URL to be HTTPS and at-or-under the issuer host (a subdomain test avoids needing a public-suffix list).
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:1047-1105` (`is_same_or_subdomain`, `validate_endpoint_domain`), applied at `:1134-1143` — "This prevents a tampered discovery response from redirecting authorization codes or client secrets to attacker-controlled servers." Issuer pre-validated at `:1006-1045`.

observed.title: Run model-proposed endpoints and values through the same untrusted-input validators as user input
observed.statement: LLM output is untrusted input: AI-proposed API endpoints still go through SSRF validation before any request; non-scalar header values are skipped loudly rather than silently dropped; the model's explicit 'skip' verdict is honored with its reason surfaced. Never let 'the AI produced it' bypass a boundary check.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/engine/credential_design.rs:203-211` (AI-produced endpoints SSRF-validated), `:230-252` — "The previous `val.as_str()`-only path silently dropped a header whose value was a number/bool ... skip genuinely non-scalar values loudly instead of silently", `:169-183` (skip verdict honored). Key-anchored extraction with negative test: `engine/src/credential_negotiator.rs:123-130`, `:308-314`.

observed.title: Single-flight an expensive probe cache by holding the lock across the recompute
observed.statement: Releasing a cache lock between the miss and the refill lets N concurrent callers all run the expensive work (subprocess fan-outs, cookie-DB copies). Hold the async mutex through the probe so late callers block briefly and then read the first caller's fresh result.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/auth_detect.rs:771-785` — "Two callers landing in the same tick (the wizard mounts multiple panels that both call this) would otherwise both see a stale/empty cache, both release the lock, and both independently spawn ~8 CLI subprocesses + copy browser cookie DBs before either writes the cache back." Lock held through `tokio::join!(probe_cli_tools(), spawn_blocking(probe_browser_cookies))`.

observed.title: Model multi-view flows as an FSM with a per-view transition allow-list
observed.statement: Encode a complex navigation flow as a discriminated-union state where each state carries exactly the data it needs, validate every action against a transition table before dispatching (invalid transitions log and no-op instead of corrupting state), and derive breadcrumbs/nav-highlight purely from the state.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/shared/hooks/useCredentialViewFSM.ts:30-47` (state union), `:88-104` (`VIEW_TRANSITIONS` + `GLOBAL_ACTIONS`), `:265-272` — `if (!isValidTransition(state.view, action.type)) { logger.warn('Invalid transition', ...); return state; }`, `:284-333` (`getBreadcrumbs` derived from state).

observed.title: Host flow follow-ups that must outlive their trigger in a module store + app-root component
observed.statement: When a flow's follow-up UI (post-save picker) must survive its parent unmounting on a view transition, keep its state in a module-level store, render the component once at app root, and let callers dispatch a promise-returning prompt(). Resolve any still-open previous prompt before opening a new one so callers can't deadlock.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/picker/resourcePickerStore.ts:1-12` — "The picker must outlive the parent form/panel that triggered it — when a Catalog form dispatches `GO_LIST` after save ... the underlying tree unmounts. A locally-mounted picker disappears with it."; `:42-52` — "if a previous prompt is still open, resolve it before opening the new one so callers don't deadlock". Host: `ResourcePickerHost.tsx`; caller hook `usePostSaveResourcePicker.tsx`.

observed.title: Consume short-lived tokens for the whole batch before any interactive pause
observed.statement: When a batch operation redeems a one-time credential/session ref per item, create all items first and only then run the interactive follow-ups — blocking on a user prompt between creates can let the short-grace-window ref expire mid-batch.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/workspace/useWorkspaceConnect.ts:71-110` — "Create ALL credentials first, without interactive pauses: the backend redeems the one-time OAuth session ref per create, and a redeemed session only survives a short grace window. Waiting on the resource picker between creates could let the ref expire mid-provisioning." — followed by a separate prompt loop.

observed.title: Give parsed rows a synthetic stable id — never key selection on a user-supplied field
observed.statement: Parsers legitimately emit duplicate keys (a repeated .env variable), so selection sets, React list keys and mapping alignment must use a generated id, not the parsed key — otherwise toggling one duplicate toggles them all and imports misalign.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/import/importHelpers.ts:64-76` — "Parsers can legitimately emit duplicate `key`s ... so `id` — not `key` — is the unique handle used for selection, React list keys, and mapping alignment."; `useCredentialImport.ts:21-22`; checkboxes keyed on `secret.id` (`ImportPreview.tsx:110-119`).

observed.title: Seed a form from props only for fields the user hasn't touched
observed.statement: When a parent passes a fresh initialValues object identity every render, a naive sync effect wipes in-progress typing. Track edited keys in a ref and only seed untouched fields from incoming props.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/forms/CredentialEditForm.tsx:80-94` — "Some callers pass a fresh `initialValues` object identity every render (e.g. `googleOAuth.getValues()`), so the effect below fires constantly — spreading initialValues LAST would wipe in-progress edits. Only seed fields the user hasn't touched." with `if (!editedFieldsRef.current.has(k)) next[k] = v;`

observed.title: Invalidate the downstream fetch cache, not just the selection, when a parent picker changes
observed.statement: In dependent/chained pickers, clearing child selections is insufficient — the fetch effect's 'already cached, skip' guard keeps serving items scoped to the old parent. Delete the cached child entries too.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/picker/ResourcePicker.tsx:142-156` — "Also clear the downstream fetch cache — otherwise the fetch effect's `if (state[spec.id]) continue` skip sees the stale cached entry and never re-fetches, so the list keeps showing items scoped to the old parent pick"; specs are topologically ordered at `:417-433`.

observed.title: Persist an explicit empty value for 'user declined', reserving null for 'never asked'
observed.statement: For optional configuration steps, save {} when the user explicitly skips, keeping null to mean never-prompted — later logic (nudges, defaults, re-prompts) can then distinguish a decision from an absence.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/picker/ResourcePicker.tsx:11-13` — "Skipping saves `{}` (distinct from never-prompted `null`) so we can tell 'user declined' from 'never shown'."; `handleSkip = () => handleCommit({})` (`:175`); read side at `features/CredentialScopeSection.tsx:19-23`.

observed.title: Flag saved selections as stale only after a confirmed successful fetch
observed.statement: Compute 'this saved pick no longer exists' only once a real response has arrived — computing during loading or after an error marks every pick stale on a transient blip. Offer an explicit one-click 'drop stale' instead of silently pruning.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/picker/ResourcePicker.tsx:224-238` — "Only computed once we have a real response (not on load or error) so a transient zero-results state doesn't flag every pick as stale." (`const stalePicks = st.fetched ? ... : []`), banner + `dropStale` at `:282-312`.

observed.title: Pin the exact serde casing of backend enums at every frontend comparison — drift disables features silently
observed.statement: A frontend string comparison against a Rust enum must match its actual serialization (no rename_all means PascalCase); a lowercase guess silently disables the whole branch. Cite the backend's serde config in a comment at each comparison site. This repo still carries a live instance of the drift: a label map keyed snake_case that always falls through to its default.
observed.detail_md: Evidence of the fix: `src/features/vault/shared/hooks/health/useRemediationEvaluator.ts:80-85` — "The Rust `Remediation` enum has no `rename_all`, so it serializes as PascalCase ('Healthy') — matching actionsForRemediation()'s switch, not the lowercase string this comparison used to check against." (same mismatch fixed twice, `:191-201`). Live anti-pattern: `features/AnomalyScorePanel.tsx:6-17` keys `REMEDIATION_LABELS` as `healthy`/`backoff_retry` (snake_case) so lookups always hit `?? REMEDIATION_LABELS.healthy`, contradicting `credentialHealthScore.ts:27-33`.

observed.title: Choose toast-vs-silent error surfacing by whether the user initiated the action
observed.statement: Background/passive reads fail silently (a toast on a poll is noise) while user-initiated actions toast — codified as named silentCatch(context)/toastCatch(context) helpers that always carry a call-site string. Passive surfaces degrade to a labelled 'unverified' state rather than blocking.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/shared/hooks/useVaultStatus.ts:12-15` — "Failures here are silent: this hook backs a passive display, not a user-triggered action, so a toast on a background poll would be noise."; `useUndoDelete.ts:23-31` — preload failure yields `eventCountVerified: false`, rendered as a warning in `CredentialDeleteDialog.tsx:46-48`. Same split across useBulkHealthcheck, ReauthBanner, BrokerPanel.

observed.title: Run the full form validation gate before every side-effecting action, not just submit
observed.statement: Test-connection, OAuth-consent and save all run the same validate() gate so a half-filled form can never start an external flow. Gate save on a passing live healthcheck only when the connector actually has one, and render the reason next to the disabled button instead of leaving a dead control.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/forms/CredentialEditForm.tsx:134-136` — handleSave/handleHealthcheck/handleOAuthConsent all `if (validate())`; `ConnectorCredentialModal.tsx:87-88,201-202` — "Connectors without a healthcheck endpoint should not block save." with `saveDisabledReason` surfaced (`FormActions.tsx:63-87`). Same rule in autoCred review: `ReviewActions.tsx:119-121,146-151` (`test_to_save` hint beside disabled save) and orchestrator-side `healthcheck_required` with documented OAuth exception (`useCredentialDesignOrchestrator.ts:112-123`).

observed.title: Secret inputs warn on paste-error smells without blocking, with explicit paste and reveal affordances
observed.statement: Secret capture rows warn (amber) on likely paste errors — too short, interior whitespace, unparsable URL — without hard-blocking submission; expose a paste button that trims; and wire the reveal toggle and errors with aria-pressed/aria-invalid/aria-describedby.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_credentials/components/forms/FieldCaptureHelpers.tsx:20-35` ("warn if too short or contains interior spaces (likely paste error)"), `:80-86` (trimming paste handler), `:127-139` (eye toggle with `aria-pressed`); `FieldCaptureRow.tsx:119-129` (`type='password'` until revealed, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`).

observed.title: Parse backend error envelopes through a typed, ordered fallback chain that never throws
observed.statement: When a backend migrates error shapes, the client parser tries structured envelope → Error.message → raw string → caller-supplied default, checks the discriminant and every field's type before trusting a shape, returns null/default for everything else, and logs (not swallows) a failed JSON parse so shape drift stays visible.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/autoCred/helpers/types.ts:113-153` — ordered chain with `silentCatch('parseAutoCredError:jsonParse')(parseErr)` breadcrumb; typed extractor `extractPendingAuthDetails` in `sub_credentials/components/gateway/PendingAuthModal.tsx:160-188` (`if (obj.kind !== 'authorization_required') return null;` + per-field `typeof` checks) with the modal kept deliberately dumb so the caller owns retry.

observed.title: Make destructive-action classifiers resolve every ambiguity as dangerous, after stripping literals
observed.statement: A heuristic guard that gates destructive execution (SQL safe mode) must fail toward 'treat as mutation': unclosed comments, unknown leading verbs, and CTE wrappers all classify as dangerous. Strip quoted literals (including dialect dollar-quoting) before keyword scanning so user data like 'please delete this' can't false-positive — and enumerate the wrapper cases where a read-only verb hides a mutation.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_databases/safeModeUtils.ts:46-48` — `if (end === -1) return true; // unclosed comment — treat as mutation (fail-safe)`; `:58` unknown verb ⇒ mutation; `:20-34,60-65` literal stripping incl. `$tag$...$tag$` plus "CTE escape hatch: a WITH query can wrap a mutation" naming the `WHERE message = 'please delete this'` false positive. Backend still enforces; the mirror is documented as UX-only (`:1-7`).

observed.title: Pin store race fixes by interleaving a deferred promise with the competing mutation
observed.statement: Slice-level concurrency bugs are testable without rendering: wire set/get around a plain object as a minimal store harness, drive the API mock with a manually-resolved deferred, start the fetch, run the competing mutation, then resolve — and assert the ghost row does not come back.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/stores/slices/vault/credentialSlice.race.test.ts:35-57` (`makeHarness()`), `:101-117` — `const fetchPromise = h.get().fetchCredentials(); await h.get().deleteCredential("X"); d.resolve([cred("A"), cred("X")]);` with "// The ghost row must NOT come back." Also steps a fake clock past the module-level fetch-cache TTL (`:75-88`, `vi.setSystemTime(clockBase + 31_000)`).

observed.title: A transport failure means the probe never ran — leave the last-known outcome alone
observed.statement: When mirroring backend check outcomes into client state, distinguish 'check ran and failed' from 'IPC/transport failed': the latter means the backend wrote nothing, so overwrite nothing. And a failing check must never erase the last-succeeded-at timestamp — that is when the credential last actually worked.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/stores/slices/vault/credentialSlice.ts:286-300` — "Only a passing check moves _success_at; a failure must not erase when the credential last actually worked." and "Transport/IPC failure — the probe never ran ... leave the stored outcome alone". Pinned by `credentialSlice.race.test.ts:186-219`.

observed.title: Give store mutations one throw contract so awaiting callers can't celebrate a failed write
observed.statement: Mutating store actions must have a consistent rethrow/swallow contract, stated in a comment: callers that gate UI transitions (close modal, navigate, toast 'Saved') on await must see a rejected backend write as a rejection — silently resolving makes the UI lie.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/stores/slices/vault/credentialSlice.ts:204-210` — "Rethrow to match createCredential's contract: callers that gate UI transitions (close modal, navigate, toast 'Saved') on await must see a rejected backend write as failure"; same at `:259-265` for field writes.

observed.title: Strip transport-only prefixed keys before persisting captured data
observed.statement: When an adapter smuggles diagnostics through the same value bag as real data, reserve a prefix (__) and filter it at the persistence boundary so debug payloads never enter the encrypted secret blob.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/autoCred/helpers/useAutoCredSession.ts:199-205` — "Strip transport-only keys (e.g. __procedure_log ...) before persisting — they aren't credential secrets and shouldn't be written into the encrypted data blob." `Object.entries(extractedValues).filter(([key]) => !key.startsWith('__'))`; reused in `steps/ReviewActions.tsx:88-90`.

observed.title: In write-only secret forms, a blank input means 'unknown', never 'clear'
observed.statement: Edit forms that never load decrypted stored secrets must submit only non-empty fields and rely on backend upsert-merge — sending blanks would wipe good secrets and hidden OAuth tokens the form could never display. Tell the user this in the UI copy.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/shared/playground/tabs/OverviewTab.tsx:74-83` — "The form never loads decrypted stored secrets, so a blank input is 'unknown', not 'cleared' — sending it would blank a good secret." with matching user-facing copy at `:64-67`.

observed.title: Put browser/agent automation behind a swappable adapter with an AbortSignal contract
observed.statement: Define automation as a narrow run(ctx, onLog, signal) interface so a stub can drive development and the real driver is one implementation. The adapter owns subprocess kill and event-listener teardown on abort — in both the abort handler and finally — so cancellation is complete regardless of which path exits.

Adapter's partial-result contract is specified MUST/SHOULD in `types.ts:33-92` and independently recomputed via `checkFieldCompleteness`.

observed.title: Label expected-miss catches with a named breadcrumb instead of a bare catch
observed.statement: Best-effort lookups (cached recipe, prefetch, saved procedure) where 'no row' is the normal case still emit a labelled breadcrumb — so a genuine IPC or shape failure is distinguishable from the expected miss when debugging production.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/autoCred/helpers/TauriPlaywrightAdapter.ts:55-59` — "No saved procedure is the expected case — fall through. Breadcrumb distinguishes shape mismatches / IPC errors from a clean 'no row'."; `design/useCredentialDesignOrchestrator.ts:56-61` (prefetch best-effort with breadcrumb + degrade to empty list); `lib/credentials/credentialRecipeRegistry.ts:125-131`.

observed.title: Escape identifiers per dialect and pin that escaping preserves printable characters
observed.statement: Identifier/glob escaping must be dialect-specific (double-quote doubling, backtick doubling, Redis glob metas) and strip only control characters — a 'sanitize to alphanumerics' regex silently corrupts legitimate names. The recorded bug: `SELECT * FROM order-items` parsed as `order MINUS items`; a Redis prefix `cache[v1]` read as a character class and silently mismatched.

Pinned by `__tests__/introspectionQueries.test.ts:7-11,42-50` and the parity suite `__tests__/introspectionParity.test.ts` (which also normalizes per-dialect column aliases like `column_type` vs `data_type` through a tiny `qr()` result factory).

observed.title: When you delete a redundant implementation, move its regression tests onto the survivor
observed.statement: Consolidating two implementations of a defence must not drop the deleted one's tests — re-point them at the remaining path so the invariant they guarded still fails loudly. Write the migration rationale into the test file header.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/vault/sub_databases/__tests__/introspectionParity.test.ts:8-18` — "The former frontend interpolated SQL builders were deleted; this test pins the rendered shape so the remaining single defense keeps producing exactly what the UI consumes — including the printable-char preservation (hyphens, spaces) the deleted builder's tests used to guard."

observed.title: Split the remediation signal bus from the action executor, with longer cooldowns for destructive actions
observed.statement: Model automated remediation as Signal → Event → Bus → Executor: the bus owns dedupe, per-action cooldown and a bounded log and knows nothing about execution; the executor is a total Record<Action, handler> where every handler is idempotent and reports its outcome back by event id. Destructive actions (auto-rotate, auto-disable) get materially longer cooldowns than advisories, and actions handled elsewhere still log an outcome so the action trail is complete.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/credentials/remediationBus.ts:50-77` — `ACTION_COOLDOWNS` (auto_rotate 15 min, auto_disable 30 min vs 5-min default), `dispatch` returns null when deduped, log capped at `MAX_LOG_SIZE`, subscriber exceptions isolated per-sub; `remediationExecutor.ts:74-111` — `ACTION_HANDLERS: Record<RemediationAction, ...>`, backoff-only actions still `updateOutcome(..., 'Backoff signal recorded')`, unknown-action fallback.

observed.title: Lock a data catalog's file shape and its cross-language seed idempotency in one test
observed.statement: For data-as-config catalogs, one vitest can pin all three layers: read the on-disk JSON and assert its exact keys, assert the accessor surfaces it, and grep the other language's seed source for the idempotency idioms (INSERT OR IGNORE, existence pre-check) — pinning 'works on fresh install' and 'works on upgrade' without any migration machinery.

WHERE id` match, under "both seed paths in the db crate root are idempotent — no new migration required".

observed.title: Persist the first successful AI derivation as a recipe shared by every entry path
observed.statement: When several UX paths need the same expensive AI-derived artifact (a connector's credential schema), persist the first successful derivation as a named recipe with a memory-cache front so later sessions skip discovery entirely — and treat recipe-cache failures as non-fatal, since caching is an optimization, not a requirement.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/lib/credentials/credentialRecipeRegistry.ts:1-8,36-49,112-116` — "Subsequent Negotiator or AutoCred sessions for the same connector skip AI discovery and reuse it." and "// Non-critical — recipe caching is an optimization, not a requirement". Three consumer paths: Design, Negotiator, AutoCred.

observed.title: A per-key cache-hit short-circuit blinds the store to set changes — compare a set signature too
observed.statement: Skipping a refetch because every key is already cached permanently hides additions, removals and backend-side changes once each id has been seen once. Also compare a sorted-id signature against the last successful fetch, and prune cache entries for ids no longer present.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/stores/slices/vault/rotationSlice.ts:44-51,89-92` — "without this, adding/removing credentials or a backend-side status change (rotation daemon) would never be picked up again once every id had been seen once" → `signature = credentials.map(c => c.id).sort().join(',')` compared to `lastFetchedCredentialSignature`; orphan pruning at `:100-110`.

observed.title: Retire IPC surfaces that carry raw token material, and leave a dated tombstone comment
observed.statement: Delete unused commands that pass secrets across a process boundary rather than leaving them 'just in case', and record the date, the hygiene rationale, and the safe shape a future implementation must take (id-based, secrets loaded backend-side) at the deletion site.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/api/vault/oauthGatewayApi.ts:58-64` — "NOTE(token-hygiene 2026-07-16): refreshOAuthToken / the refresh_oauth_token command were retired — the command was the only OAuth IPC surface that accepted a raw refresh_token (and returned raw tokens), and it had no caller. ... If a UI-driven refresh is ever needed, add a credential-id-based command that loads the token backend-side."

observed.title: Classify reachability-sweep verdicts by intent: non-auth 4xx is a pass
observed.statement: A batch endpoint-reachability test should treat 400/404/422 as passed (the server responded, auth worked, the endpoint exists) and only 401/403/5xx as failed; endpoints it cannot construct (unresolved path params) are pre-marked skipped with the reason in the result rather than silently omitted.

observed.title: Reconcile a failed optimistic delete by re-fetching, not by re-appending
observed.statement: On rollback of an optimistic removal, prefer re-fetching the scoped list — a concurrent fetch may already have restored the item, so re-appending duplicates it. Only splice the item back (guarded by an id-presence check) when no scope key exists to re-fetch by.

observed.title: Keep security-reassurance badges live, control-free, and honest about their own gaps
observed.statement: A green 'vault secured' badge is a display, never a control (no 'encrypt now' button — the guarantee is automatic); it must reflect the actual variant in force (keychain vs machine-derived fallback), flip amber when a subsidiary guarantee fails (missed audit writes), and stay live via a slow poll plus refresh-on-focus — a mount-only fetch left it permanently green through a live failure.

There is intentionally NO 'encrypt now' button"; `:32-45` — "Mount-only fetch left the badge permanently green while the tab stayed open — an audit-write failure during a live run never flipped it amber until a remount (2026-07-16 UAT T-1)"; `:49-58` — non-zero missed-audit count "an honesty signal this badge must not hide behind a green shield".

observed.title: Surface probably-forgotten API keys with a two-window staleness heuristic
observed.statement: Flag an active key as stale when it is older than a creation grace window AND either never used or unused beyond an inactivity window — surfacing forgotten keys as an amber chip with a tooltip, not an auto-revoke. Keep both thresholds as named module constants so the knob is one obvious edit.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/settings/sub_api_keys/components/ApiKeysSettings.tsx:44-60` — `STALE_GRACE_DAYS = 7`, `STALE_INACTIVE_DAYS = 30`, "Pulled out so the threshold is one obvious knob to tune later"; `isStaleKey` excludes revoked/disabled keys and treats unparsable dates as not-stale; rendered as an amber `stale_chip` with tooltip (`:361-369`).

observed.title: Gate remote-app pairing on an explicit approval that mints an origin-bound, scoped, expiring key
observed.statement: Nothing is minted from a pairing request without the user's click: the approval modal defaults scopes to exactly what was requested but lets the user narrow them, offers only bounded expiry options, warns visibly on a non-HTTPS origin, and arms the Approve button after a short delay so a stray double-tap can't grant remote access. The minted key is bound to the requesting origin and claimed once.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/settings/sub_api_keys/components/PairApprovalModal.tsx:1-7` — "nothing is minted without the user's click. On approve, the backend mints an origin-bound, scoped, expiring key the cloud app claims once"; `:22-25` `APPROVE_ARM_DELAY_MS = 450` ("approving grants a remote origin access"); `:69,114-119` non-HTTPS warning; `:54-64` per-request reset defaults scopes to the requested set. Paired keys render in their own 'Connected apps' section with disconnect (`ApiKeysSettings.tsx:169-171,264-285`).

observed.title: Store API keys as hashes with a display prefix, and separate audit-preserving revoke from delete
observed.statement: The plaintext token leaves the backend exactly once at creation (behind an 'I have stored it' acknowledgment); at rest only the SHA-256 lives in the row, with a short key_prefix column for UI recognition. Revoke flips a flag so the audit trail survives; delete removes the row — two distinct actions with distinct affordances. The app's own internal system key is hidden from the user-facing list entirely.
observed.detail_md: Evidence: `src/features/settings/sub_api_keys/components/ApiKeysSettings.tsx:10-18` — "Plaintext token leaves the backend exactly ONCE on creation ... Stored as SHA-256; revoke flips a flag (audit trail), delete removes the row. The per-row 'system' key is the desktop frontend's own internal key ... We hide it from the user-facing list — it isn't theirs to manage." (`HIDDEN_KEY_NAMES`, `:75,112`); prefix display `{apiKey.key_prefix}…` (`:385`); per-key request audit drawer via `list_api_key_audit` (`ApiKeyAuditDrawer.tsx:1-6`).
